title: حِكَايَةُ نُورِ الدِّينِ وَشَمْسِ الدِّينِ
titleEn: The Three Apples, concluded; Nūr al-Dīn and Shams al-Dīn
part: Night 20 · The Three Apples ends / The Tale of Nūr al-Dīn and Shams al-Dīn begins
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 147–154 (Night 20, continuing directly from nights-19), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm exactly as Macnaghten prints it. Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition's Middle Arabic forms and its occasional compositor's slips, is preserved unaltered; a few genuinely obscure or corrupt-looking forms are vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes rather than silently repaired. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 20 closes the tale of the three apples. Jaʿfar, on the verge of hanging, finds the fatal apple in his little daughter's pocket and learns from the slave Rayḥān how it came to him; the caliph, amazed, is promised a tale still stranger — the history of the viziers Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī and Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad of Egypt. The two brothers quarrel over the marriage-portion of their unborn children; Nūr al-Dīn, stung, rides away alone to Basra, where the old vizier takes him in and gives him his daughter. Verse is copied as printed. Dawn cuts Shahrazad off as the bridegroom comes out of the bath. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularized the language here and there, so some of the original Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْعِشْرُونَ قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-ʿishrūna qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu
sentences.l: So when was the night the-twentieth, she-said: It-reached-me, O king the-fortunate,
sentences.i: When it was the twentieth night, she said: It has reached me, fortunate king,

sentences.t: أَنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ حَلَفَ أَنَّهُ لَا يَشْنُقُ إِلَّا الْعَبْدَ فَإِنَّ الشَّابَّ مَعْذُورٌ
sentences.tr: anna al-khalīfata ḥalafa annahu lā yashnuqu illā al-ʿabda fa-inna al-shābba maʿdhūrun
sentences.l: that the caliph swore that-he not hangs except the slave; for indeed the youth is excused.
sentences.i: that the caliph had sworn he would hang no one but the slave, since the young man was blameless.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْخَلِيفَةَ الْتَفَتَ إِلَى جَعْفَرٍ وَقَالَ لَهُ أَحْضِرْ لِي هَذَا الْعَبْدَ الْمَلْعُونَ الَّذِي جَرَتْ مِنْهُ هَذِهِ الْقَضِيَّةُ وَإِنْ لَمْ تُحْضِرْهُ فَأَنْتَ عِوَضُهُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-khalīfata iltafata ilā Jaʿfarin wa-qāla lahu aḥḍir lī hādhā al-ʿabda al-malʿūna alladhī jarat minhu hādhihi al-qaḍiyyatu wa-in lam tuḥḍirhu fa-anta ʿiwaḍuhu
sentences.l: Then indeed the caliph turned to Jaʿfar and said to-him: Bring to-me this slave the-cursed, who occurred from-him this affair; and if not you-bring-him, then you are his-replacement.
sentences.i: Then the caliph turned to Jaʿfar and said to him: Bring me this accursed slave, from whom this affair arose; and if you do not bring him, you shall be his substitute.
sentences.n: إِنَّ after ثُمَّ simply re-opens the narrative ("then indeed"); it need not be translated. جَرَتْ مِنْهُ is literally "ran from him", i.e. originated with him.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَ جَعْفَرٌ يَبْكِي وَيَقُولُ حَضِّرْ لِي مَوْتَتَيْنِ وَلَا كُلَّ مَرَّةٍ تَسْلَمُ الْجَرَّةُ
sentences.tr: fa-nazala Jaʿfarun yabkī wa-yaqūlu ḥaḍḍir lī mawtatayni wa-lā kulla marratin taslamu al-jarratu
sentences.l: So went-down Jaʿfar weeping and saying: Prepare for-me two-deaths; and not every time is-safe the jar.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar went down weeping and saying: Make ready two deaths for me; the jar does not come through whole every time.
sentences.n: The printed حضر is bare and could be حَضَّرَ "he prepared" or the imperative حَضِّرْ; it is read here as the imperative, a bitter jest ("get two deaths ready for me"). وَلَا كُلَّ مَرَّةٍ تَسْلَمُ الْجَرَّةُ is the proverb that the pitcher does not survive every trip to the well. The reading of the whole line is uncertain.

sentences.t: وَ لَيْسَ فِي هَذَا الْأَمْرِ حِيلَةٌ وَالَّذِي سَلَّمَنِي فِى الْأَوَّلِ يُسَلِّمُنِي فِى الثَّانِي
sentences.tr: wa-laysa fī hādhā al-amri ḥīlatun wa-alladhī sallamanī fī al-awwali yusallimunī fī al-thānī
sentences.l: And there-is-not in this matter a-stratagem; and the-one-who saved-me in the first will-save-me in the second.
sentences.i: There is no stratagem in this matter; he who saved me the first time will save me the second.

sentences.t: وَاللهِ مَا بَقِيتُ أَخْرُجُ مِنْ بَيْتِي ثَلَٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَالْحَقُّ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ
sentences.tr: wa-Allāhi mā baqītu akhruju min baytī thalāthata ayyāmin wa-al-Ḥaqqu yafʿalu mā yashāʾu
sentences.l: By-God, not I-remained going-out from my-house three days; and the-Real does what He-wills.
sentences.i: By God, I will not set foot outside my house for three days; and God does what He wills.
sentences.n: مَا بَقِيتُ أَخْرُجُ ("I did not remain going out") is a Middle Arabic idiom of resolve: "I shall not go out any more." الْحَقُّ "the Real, the True" is one of the names of God.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَقَامَ فِي بَيْتِهِ ثَلَٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ وَفِي الْيَوْمِ الرَّابِعِ أَحْضَرَ الْقُضَاةَ وَالشُّهُودَ وَوَدَّعَ أَوْلَادَهُ وَهُوَ يَبْكِي
sentences.tr: thumma aqāma fī baytihi thalāthata ayyāmin wa-fī al-yawmi al-rābiʿi aḥḍara al-quḍāta wa-al-shuhūda wa-waddaʿa awlādahu wa-huwa yabkī
sentences.l: Then he-stayed in his-house three days, and on the day the-fourth he-summoned the judges and the witnesses and bade-farewell-to his-children, and he weeping.
sentences.i: Then he stayed in his house for three days, and on the fourth day he summoned the judges and the witnesses and bade his children farewell, weeping.

sentences.t: وَإِذَا بِرَسُولِ الْخَلِيفَةِ أَتَى إِلَيْهِ وَقَالَ لَهُ إِنَّ أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ فِي أَشَدِّ مَا يَكُونُ مِنَ الْغَضَبِ وَأَرْسَلَ بِطَلَبِكَ وَحَلَفَ أَنَّهُ لَا يَمُرُّ هَذَا النَّهَارُ إِلَّا وَأَنْتَ مَشْنُوقٌ
sentences.tr: wa-idhā bi-rasūli al-khalīfati atā ilayhi wa-qāla lahu inna amīra al-muʾminīna fī ashaddi mā yakūnu min al-ghaḍabi wa-arsala bi-ṭalabika wa-ḥalafa annahu lā yamurru hādhā al-nahāru illā wa-anta mashnūqun
sentences.l: And behold, a-messenger of-the-caliph came to-him and said to-him: Indeed the Commander of-the-Faithful is in the-most-severe of-what can-be of anger, and has-sent for-your-summons, and has-sworn that-not passes this day except and you hanged.
sentences.i: And behold, a messenger from the caliph came to him and said: The Commander of the Faithful is in the most terrible rage that can be, and he has sent for you; he has sworn that this day shall not pass but you will be hanged.
sentences.n: وَإِذَا بِـ "and behold": بِـ after إِذَا of surprise only marks what appears. أَرْسَلَ بِطَلَبِكَ is "sent with a demand for you", i.e. sent to summon you. إِلَّا وَأَنْتَ مَشْنُوقٌ: the وَ introduces a circumstantial clause ("without you being hanged").

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ جَعْفَرٌ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ بَكَى وَبَكَوْا أَوْلَادُهُ وَعَبِيدُهُ مَعَ كُلِّ مَنْ فِى الدَّارِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Jaʿfarun hādhā al-kalāma bakā wa-bakaw awlāduhu wa-ʿabīduhu maʿa kulli man fī al-dāri
sentences.l: So when heard Jaʿfar this speech he-wept, and wept his-children and his-slaves with every one-who in the house.
sentences.i: When Jaʿfar heard these words he wept, and his children and servants wept with everyone in the house.
sentences.n: بَكَوْا precedes its plural subject أَوْلَادُهُ: the verb agrees in the plural, as in Middle Arabic and the colloquials, where Classical Arabic would keep it singular.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنَ التَّوْدِيعِ تَقَدَّمَ إِىٰ بِنْتِهِ الصَّغِيرَةِ لِيُوَدِّعَهَا وَكَانَ يُحِبُّهَا أَكْثَرَ مِنْ أَوْلَادِهِ جَمِيعًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min al-tawdīʿi taqaddama ilā bintihi al-ṣaghīrati li-yuwaddiʿahā wa-kāna yuḥibbuhā akthara min awlādihi jamīʿan
sentences.l: So when he-finished from the bidding-farewell he-approached to his-daughter the-little, to-bid-her-farewell; and he-was loving-her more than his-children all.
sentences.i: When he had finished the farewells he went up to his little daughter to bid her farewell, for he loved her more than all his other children.
sentences.n: The edition prints اى (without lam) for إِلَى "to"; it is read ilā here and in the next sentence but one. لِيُوَدِّعَهَا: لِـ with a subjunctive verb gives purpose, "in order to bid her farewell".

sentences.t: فَضَمَّهَا إِىٰ صَدْرِهِ وَبَاسَهَا وَبَكَى عَلَى فِرَاقِهَا فَوَجَدَ فِي جَيْبِهَا شَيْئًا مُكَتَّبًا
sentences.tr: fa-ḍammahā ilā ṣadrihi wa-bāsahā wa-bakā ʿalā firāqihā fa-wajada fī jaybihā shayʾan mukattaban
sentences.l: So he-pressed-her to his-chest and kissed-her and wept over parting-from-her, and found in her-pocket a-thing inscribed.
sentences.i: He clasped her to his chest and kissed her and wept over parting from her, and found something inscribed in her pocket.
sentences.n: مُكَتَّبًا is printed مكتبا, without the waw of مَكْتُوبًا; it is read as the form II participle "inscribed, written upon", which fits the sense.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهَا مَا الَّذِي فِي جَيْبِكِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahā mā alladhī fī jaybiki
sentences.l: So he-said to-her: What the-thing-which is in your-pocket?
sentences.i: He said to her: What is that in your pocket?

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُ يَا أَبَتِ تُفَّاحَةٌ مَكْتُوبٌ عَلَيْهَا اسْمُ مَوْلَانَا الْخَلِيفَةِ جَاءَ بِهَا عَبْدُنَا رَيْحَانُ وَلَهَا مَعِي أَرْبَعَةُ أَيَّامٍ وَمَا أَعْطَا هَانِي حَتَّى أَخَذَ مِنِّي دِينَارَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahu yā abati tuffāḥatun maktūbun ʿalayhā ismu mawlānā al-khalīfati jāʾa bihā ʿabdunā Rayḥānu wa-lahā maʿī arbaʿatu ayyāmin wa-mā aʿṭā hānī ḥattā akhadha minnī dīnārayni
sentences.l: So she-said to-him: O my-father, an-apple, written upon-it the-name of-our-master the-caliph; brought it our-slave Rayḥān; and for-it with-me four days; and not he-gave it-me until he-took from-me two-dinars.
sentences.i: She said to him: Father, it is an apple with the name of our lord the caliph written on it. Our slave Rayḥān brought it; it has been with me four days, and he would not give it to me until he had taken two dinars from me.
sentences.n: يَا أَبَتِ is the vocative "my father" with the ـتِ of address (the edition prints it with ت). أَعْطَا هَانِي is two printed words: أَعْطَا (spelled with alif for أَعْطَى) and هَانِي, the pronouns "it" and "me" run together in the colloquial order -hā-nī; the whole is read aʿṭā-hā-nī "he gave it to me". جَاءَ بِهَا: the verb جَاءَ takes بِـ for "bring" ("come with").

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ جَعْفَرٌ بِذَلِكَ الْعَبْدِ وَالتُّفَّاحَةِ فَرِحَ وَحَطَّ يَدَهُ فِي جَيْبِ ابْنَتِهِ وَأَخْرَجَ التُّفَّاحَةَ فَعَرَفَهَا وَقَالَ يَا قَرِيبَ الْفَرَجِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Jaʿfarun bi-dhālika al-ʿabdi wa-al-tuffāḥati fariḥa wa-ḥaṭṭa yadahu fī jaybi ibnatihi wa-akhraja al-tuffāḥata fa-ʿarafahā wa-qāla yā qarība al-farajī
sentences.l: So when heard Jaʿfar of that slave and the apple he-rejoiced, and put his-hand in the pocket of-his-daughter and brought-out the apple, and knew-it, and said: O near-one of-the-relief!
sentences.i: When Jaʿfar heard of that slave and the apple he rejoiced; he put his hand into his daughter's pocket, drew out the apple and recognised it, and said: O You who are near with relief!
sentences.n: سَمِعَ بِـ is "hear of, hear about". يَا قَرِيبَ الْفَرَجِ is an invocation of God, "O near-in-relief"; the vocative noun is in construct, hence the accusative قَرِيبَ.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَمَرَ بِإِحْضَارِ الْعَبْدِ فَحَضَرَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu amara bi-iḥḍāri al-ʿabdi fa-ḥaḍara
sentences.l: Then indeed-he commanded the-bringing of-the-slave, and he-came.
sentences.i: Then he ordered the slave to be brought, and the slave came.
sentences.n: أَمَرَ بِـ "command (something)": the verb takes بِـ before the verbal noun إِحْضَارِ.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ وَيْلَكَ رَيْحَانُ مِنْ أَيْنَ لَكَ هَذِهِ التُّفَّاحَةُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu waylaka Rayḥānu min ayna laka hādhihi al-tuffāḥatu
sentences.l: So he-said to-him: Woe-to-you, Rayḥān! From where to-you this apple?
sentences.i: He said to him: Woe to you, Rayḥān! Where did you get this apple?
sentences.n: مِنْ أَيْنَ لَكَ is "from where (is) to you", the ordinary way to ask how one comes to possess something.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْعَبْدُ وَاللهِ يَا سَيِّدِي إِنْ كَانَ الْكَذِبُ أَنْجَا فَالصِّدْقُ أَنْجَا وَأَنْجَا هَذِهِ التُّفَّاحَةُ مَا سَرَقْتُهَا لَا مِنْ قَصْرِكَ وَلَا مِنْ قَصْرِ الْحَضْرَةِ وَلَا مِنْ بُسْتَانِ أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ʿabdu wa-Allāhi yā sayyidī in kāna al-kadhibu anjā fa-al-ṣidqu anjā wa-anjā hādhihi al-tuffāḥatu mā saraqtuhā lā min qaṣrika wa-lā min qaṣri al-ḥaḍrati wa-lā min bustāni amīri al-muʾminīna
sentences.l: So said the-slave: By-God, O my-master, if was the-lying more-saving, then the-truth is more-saving; and more-saving still: this apple, not I-stole-it, neither from your-palace nor from the palace of-the-Presence nor from the garden of-the-Commander of-the-Faithful.
sentences.i: The slave said: By God, my lord, if lying saves, truth saves still more; and what is more, this apple I did not steal, neither from your palace, nor from the palace of the Presence, nor from the garden of the Commander of the Faithful.
sentences.n: أَنْجَا is printed with alif for أَنْجَى "more saving" (a comparative of نَجَا "be saved"); the construction of the saying is obscure and the middle clause (وَأَنْجَا) is read as an aside, "and more saving still". الْحَضْرَةُ "the Presence" is a respectful circumlocution for the caliph or his court.

sentences.t: وَ إِنَّمَا هَذِهِ مِنْ مُدَّةِ خَمْسَةِ أَيَّامٍ مَشَيْتُ فَدَخَلْتُ إِلَى بَعْضِ أَزِقَّةِ الْمَدِينَةِ فَنَظَرْتُ صِغَارًا يَلْعَبُونَ وَمَعَ وَاحِدٍ مِنْهُمْ هَذِهِ التُّفَّاحَةُ
sentences.tr: wa-innamā hādhihi min muddati khamsati ayyāmin mashaytu fa-dakhaltu ilā baʿḍi al-azziqqati al-madīnati fa-naẓartu ṣighāran yalʿabūna wa-maʿa wāḥidin minhum hādhihi al-tuffāḥatu
sentences.l: And it-is-only that from a-period of-five days I-walked, and entered into some of-the-lanes of-the-city, and saw children playing, and with one of-them this apple.
sentences.i: The fact is, five days ago I was walking, and I went into one of the lanes of the city and saw some children playing, and one of them had this apple.
sentences.n: مِنْ مُدَّةِ خَمْسَةِ أَيَّامٍ is "from a period of five days", i.e. five days ago.

sentences.t: فَخَطَفْتُهَا مِنْهُ وَضَرَبْتُهُ فَبَكَى وَقَالَ يَا فَتَى هَذِهِ لِأُمِّي وَهِيَ مَرِيضَةٌ وَقَدِ اشْتَهَتْ عَلَى أَبِى التُّفَّاحَةَ فَسَافَرَ إِلَى الْبَصْرَةِ وَجَاءَ لَهَا ثَلَٰثَ تُفَّاحَاتٍ بِثَلَٰثَةِ دَنَانِيرَ فَسَرَقْتُ مِنْهُمْ وَاحِدَةً أَلْعَبُ بِهَا
sentences.tr: fa-khaṭaftuhā minhu wa-ḍarabtuhu fa-bakā wa-qāla yā fatā hādhihi li-ummī wa-hiya marīḍatun wa-qadi ishtahat ʿalā abī al-tuffāḥata fa-sāfara ilā al-Baṣrati wa-jāʾa lahā thalātha tuffāḥātin bi-thalāthati danānīra fa-saraqtu minhum wāḥidatan alʿabu bihā
sentences.l: So I-snatched-it from-him and struck-him, and he-wept and said: O young-man, this is for-my-mother, and she ill, and she-has craved of my-father the apple; so he-travelled to Basra and brought for-her three apples for three dinars; so I-stole from-them one, I-play with-it.
sentences.i: I snatched it from him and struck him, and he wept and said: Young man, this is for my mother, and she is ill; she craved an apple and asked my father for it, so he travelled to Basra and brought her three apples for three dinars, and I stole one of them to play with.
sentences.n: The speech here is the child's. لِأُمِّي: لِـ "for" + أُمّ "mother" + ـي "my". اشْتَهَتْ عَلَى أَبِى is literally "she craved upon my father", i.e. she demanded of him what she craved. أَلْعَبُ بِهَا ("I play with it") is a bare imperfect after the object, expressing purpose without any particle. The pointing of بِثَلَٰثَةِ دَنَانِيرَ: دَنَانِيرَ is diptote, hence the fatḥa.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ بَكَى فَامَ الْتَفَتُّ إِلَيْهِ وَأَخَذْتُهَا وَجِئْتُ هُنَا فَأَخَذَتْهَا سِتِّي الصَّغِيرَةُ بِدِينَارَيْنِ ذَهَبٍ
sentences.tr: thumma bakā fa-mā iltafattu ilayhi wa-akhadhtuhā wa-jiʾtu hunā fa-akhadhathā sittī al-ṣaghīratu bi-dīnārayni dhahabin
sentences.l: Then he-wept, and not I-turned to-him; and I-took-it and came here, and took-it my-lady the-little for two-dinars of-gold.
sentences.i: Then he wept, but I paid him no heed; I took it and came here, and my little lady bought it from me for two gold dinars.
sentences.n: The edition prints فام, evidently a misprint with the letters reversed for فَمَا "and not"; it is read fa-mā iltafattu "and I did not turn". سِتِّي "my lady" is the colloquial form of سَيِّدَتِي. أَخَذَتْهَا بِدِينَارَيْنِ: أَخَذَ "take" with بِـ of price, "for two dinars", i.e. she took it from him by paying two dinars (the slave takes the price).

sentences.t: وَهَذِهِ حِكَايَتِي
sentences.tr: wa-hādhihi ḥikāyatī
sentences.l: And this is my-story.
sentences.i: And that is my story.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ جَعْفَرٌ هَذِهِ الْقِصَّةَ تَعَجَّبَ لِكَوْنِ أَنَّ الْفِتْنَةَ وَقَتْلَ الصَّبِيَّةِ مِنْ عَبْدِهِ وَحَزِنَ لِنِسْبَةِ الْعَبْدِ لَهُ وَفَرِحَ لِخَلَاصِ نَفْسِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Jaʿfarun hādhihi al-qiṣṣata taʿajjaba li-kawni anna al-fitnata wa-qatla al-ṣabiyyati min ʿabdihi wa-ḥazina li-nisbati al-ʿabdi lahu wa-fariḥa li-khalāṣi nafsihi
sentences.l: So when heard Jaʿfar this tale he-marvelled at-the-being that the strife and the killing of-the-girl were from his-slave, and grieved at-the-attribution of-the-slave to-him, and rejoiced at-the-deliverance of-himself.
sentences.i: When Jaʿfar heard this tale he marvelled that the strife and the killing of the girl had come from his own slave; he grieved that the slave was his, and rejoiced that he himself was delivered.
sentences.n: لِكَوْنِ أَنَّ is "because of the fact that"; لِـ here gives the cause of his wonder, as it does for حَزِنَ لِـ and فَرِحَ لِـ. نِسْبَة is the relation or attribution: the slave belonged to him.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَنْشَدَ يَقُولُ شِعْرًا
sentences.tr: thumma anshada yaqūlu shiʿran
sentences.l: Then he-recited, saying, poetry:
sentences.i: Then he recited these verses:

sentences.t:
اِذَا جَاءَ الْمُصِيْبَةُ فِيْ غُلَامٍ * فَتَجْعَلُهُ لِنَفْسِكَ مِنْ فِدَاهَا
فَاِنَّكَ وَاجِدٌ خَدَمًا كَثِيْرًا * وَنَفْسُكَ لَمْ تَجِدْ نَفْسًا سِوَاهَا
sentences.tr:
idhā jāʾa al-muṣībatu fī ghulāmin * fa-tajʿaluhu li-nafsika min fidāhā
fa-innaka wājidun khadaman kathīran * wa-nafsuka lam tajid nafsan siwāhā
sentences.l:
If came the-calamity in a-servant, * then you-make-him for-yourself from its-ransom,
then indeed-you finding servants many, * and your-self not you-find a-self besides-it.
sentences.i: If calamity strikes through a servant, then count him among its ransoms for your own life; for you will find many servants, but you will never find another self besides your own.
sentences.n: The edition points its verse and the pointing is kept as printed. جَاءَ الْمُصِيْبَةُ has a masculine verb before a feminine subject, which is allowed when the verb comes first. The meaning is that a servant is a fit ransom for one's own life. The couplet rhymes on -hā.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ مَسَكَ بِيَدِ الْعَبْدِ وَطَلَعَ بِهِ لِلْخَلِيفَةِ وَحَكَى لَهُ قِصَّتَهُ مِنْ أَوَّلِهَا إِلَى آخِرِهَا فَتَعَجَّبَ الْخَلِيفَةُ كُلَّ الْعَجَبِ وَضَحِكَ حَتَّى انْقَلَبَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu masaka bi-yadi al-ʿabdi wa-ṭalaʿa bihi li-al-khalīfati wa-ḥakā lahu qiṣṣatahu min awwalihā ilā ākhirihā fa-taʿajjaba al-khalīfatu kulla al-ʿajabi wa-ḍaḥika ḥattā inqalaba
sentences.l: Then indeed-he took-hold with-the-hand of-the-slave, and went-up with-him to-the-caliph, and told to-him his-story from its-first to its-last; so the-caliph marvelled all the-marvelling, and laughed until he-toppled-over.
sentences.i: Then he took the slave by the hand and went up with him to the caliph, and told him the whole story from beginning to end. The caliph marvelled exceedingly, and laughed until he fell over backwards.

sentences.t: وَ أَمَرَانْ تُؤَرَّخَ هَذِهِ الْحِكَايَةُ وَتُجْعَلَ سِيَرًا بَيْنَ النَّاسِ
sentences.tr: wa- amara an tuʾarrakha hādhihi al-ḥikāyatu wa-tujʿala siyaran bayna al-nāsi
sentences.l: And he-ordered that be-recorded this the-tale, and be-made chronicles among the-people.
sentences.i: And he commanded that this tale be set down in the annals and made a chronicle among the people.
sentences.n: The و stands alone at the end of one printed line and أمران begins the next, and أمران is two words run together: أَمَرَ أَنْ "he ordered that". The vowelling shows both (أَمَرَانْ is read amara an). تُؤَرَّخَ is passive: "that this tale be dated, set down in the annals"; the hamza seat is the printed و.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَا تَعْجَبْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْقِصَّةِ فَمَاهِيَ أَعْجَبُ مِنْ حَدِيثِ الْوَزِيرِ نُورِالدِّينِ عَلِيٍّ الْمِصْرِيِّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lā taʿjab yā amīra al-muʾminīna min hādhihi al-qiṣṣati fa-mā hiya aʿjabu min ḥadīthi al-wazīri Nūri al-Dīni ʿAlīyin al-Miṣrī
sentences.l: So he-said: "Do-not marvel, O Commander of-the-Faithful, at this the-story, for-not it more-marvellous than the-account of-the-vizier Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī the-Egyptian."
sentences.i: Jaʿfar said, "Commander of the Faithful, do not marvel at this story, for it is no stranger than the tale of the vizier Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī of Egypt."
sentences.n: Here and below نورالدين is printed as one word; it is read as the construct Nūr al-Dīn ("Light of the Faith"), with the case ending on the first half.

sentences.t: حِكَايَةُ الْوَزِيرِ نُورِ الدِّينِ وَأَخِيهِ وَشَمْسِ الدِّينِ مُحَمَّدٍ أَخِيهِ
sentences.tr: ḥikāyatu al-wazīri Nūri al-Dīni wa-akhīhi wa-Shamsi al-Dīni Muḥammadin akhīhi
sentences.l: The-tale of-the-vizier Nūr al-Dīn and-his-brother and-Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad his-brother.
sentences.i: The Tale of the Vizier Nūr al-Dīn and His Brother Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad
sentences.n: This is a run-in heading, printed in the middle of the line in the midst of the dialogue; it opens the tale Jaʿfar is about to tell. It is read as a title in the genitive, as in the other tale headings.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْخَلِيفَةُ هَاتِ وَمَا الَّتِي أَعْجَبُ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْحِكَايَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-khalīfatu hāti wa-mā allatī aʿjabu min hādhihi al-ḥikāyati
sentences.l: So said the-caliph: "Bring! And what the-one-that more-marvellous than this the-tale?"
sentences.i: The caliph said, "Tell it! And what is it that is stranger than this tale?"
sentences.n: هَاتِ is the imperative "bring (it)": here "out with it!".

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرُ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ لَا أُحَدِّثُكَ إِلَّا بِشَرْطٍ أَنْ تُعْتِقَ عَبْدِي مِنَ الْقَتْلِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfaru yā amīra al-muʾminīna lā uḥaddithuka illā bi-sharṭin an tuʿtiqa ʿabdī mina al-qatli
sentences.l: So said Jaʿfar: "O Commander of-the-Faithful, not I-relate-to-you except with-a-condition: that you-free my-slave from the-killing."
sentences.i: Jaʿfar said, "Commander of the Faithful, I will tell you only on one condition: that you spare my slave from death."

sentences.t: فَقَالَ إِنْ كَانَ أَعْجَبَ مِمَّا اتَّفَقَ لَنَا وَهَبْتُ دَمَهُ لَكَ وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ بِأ عْجَبَ قَتَلْتُ عَبْدَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla in kāna aʿjaba mimmā ittafaqa lanā wahabtu damahu laka wa-in lam yakun bi-a ʿjaba qataltu ʿabdaka
sentences.l: So he-said: "If it-be more-marvellous than-that-which befell us, I-grant his-blood to-you; and if not it-be more-marvellous, I-kill your-slave."
sentences.i: The caliph said, "If it is stranger than what befell us, I will give you his blood; and if it is not stranger, I will kill your slave."
sentences.n: The edition prints با عجب with a space inside the word: it is بِأَعْجَبَ, "more marvellous", with the preposition بِـ that follows a negated كان. It is vowelled as printed, bi-a + ʿjaba.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ جَعْفَرُ اِعْلَمْ يَا أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ أَنَّهُ كَانَ فِي سَالِفِ الزَّمَانِ بِأَرْضِ مِصْرَ سُلْطَانٌ صَاحِبُ عَدْلٍ وَأَمَانٍ يُحِبُّ الْفُقَرَاءَ وَيُجَالِسُ الْعُلَمَاءَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Jaʿfaru iʿlam yā amīra al-muʾminīna annahu kāna fī sālifi al-zamāni bi-arḍi Miṣra sulṭānun ṣāḥibu ʿadlin wa-amānin yuḥibbu al-fuqarāʾa wa-yujālisu al-ʿulamāʾa
sentences.l: So said Jaʿfar: "Know, O Commander of-the-Faithful, that-he was in the-past-time, in-the-land of-Egypt, a-sultan, possessor-of justice and-security, loving the-poor and-sitting-with the-learned.
sentences.i: Jaʿfar said, "Know, Commander of the Faithful, that in time long past there was in the land of Egypt a sultan, a man of justice and security, who loved the poor and kept company with the learned.

sentences.t: وَلَهُ وَزِيرٌ عَاقِلٌ خَبِيرٌ لَهُ عِلْمٌ بِالْأُمُورِ وَالتَّدْبِيرِ
sentences.tr: wa-lahu wazīrun ʿāqilun khabīrun lahu ʿilmun bi-al-umūri wa-al-tadbīri
sentences.l: And-to-him a-vizier, wise, experienced; to-him knowledge of-the-affairs and-the-management.
sentences.i: He had a vizier, wise and well-versed, who knew affairs and their management.
sentences.n: The pair عَاقِلٌ خَبِيرٌ and الْأُمُورِ وَالتَّدْبِيرِ show the light sajʿ-like pairing of the opening formula.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا وَلَهُ وَلَدَ انِ كَأَنَّهُمَا قَمَرَانِ لَمْ يُرَ مِثْلُهُمَا فِى الْحُسْنِ وَالْجَمَالِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna shaykhan kabīran wa-lahu waladāni ka-annahumā qamarāni lam yura mithluhumā fī al-ḥusni wa-al-jamāli
sentences.l: And he-was an-old-man, aged; and-to-him two-sons, as-though-they two-moons, not was-seen the-like-of-them in beauty and-loveliness.
sentences.i: He was an aged elder, and he had two sons who were like two moons; their like was never seen for beauty and loveliness.
sentences.n: ولد ان is printed with a space; read as the dual وَلَدَانِ "two sons", and so the second part is vowelled انِ. كأنهما is كَأَنَّ + the dual pronoun: ka-, "like, as if" + anna + humā.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ اسْمُ الْكَبِيرِ شَمْسُ الدِّينِ مُحَمَّدٌ وَاسْمُ الصَّغِيرِ نُورُالدِّينِ عَلِيٌّ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna ismu al-kabīri Shamsu al-Dīni Muḥammadun wa-ismu al-ṣaghīri Nūru al-Dīni ʿAlīyun
sentences.l: And was the-name of-the-elder Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad, and-the-name of-the-younger Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī.
sentences.i: The elder was named Shams al-Dīn Muḥammad and the younger Nūr al-Dīn ʿAlī.
sentences.n: Classical would put the names after كان in the accusative; the names are left in the nominative here, as a quoted name.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الصَّغِيرُ أَمْيَزَ مِنَ الْكَبِيرِ فِى الصَّبَاحَةِ وَالْمَلَاحَةِ حَتَّى أَنَّ فِي بَعْضِ الْبُلْدَانِ تَسَامَعُوا بِهِ فَسَافَرُوا إِلَى بِلَادِهِ لِأَجْلِ رُؤْيَةِ جَمَالِهِ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-ṣaghīru amyaza mina al-kabīri fī al-ṣabāḥati wa-al-malāḥati ḥattā anna fī baʿḍi al-buldāni tasāmaʿū bihi fa-sāfarū ilā bilādihi li-ajli ruʾyati jamālihi
sentences.l: And was the-younger more-distinguished than the-elder in radiance and-comeliness, so-that in some of-the-lands they-heard-of-one-another about-him, and-they-travelled to his-country for-the-sake of-the-seeing of-his-beauty.
sentences.i: The younger was more distinguished than the elder in radiance and comeliness, so much so that in certain lands people heard tell of him and travelled to his country to see his beauty.
sentences.n: الصباحة والملاحة is a rhyming pair (both "comeliness"). تسامعوا is form VI, "they heard of him from one another": the news passed by word of mouth.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ أَنَّ وَالِدَهُمْ مَاتَ فَحَزِنَ عَلَيْهِ السُّلْطَانُ وَأَقْبَلَ عَلَى الْوَلَدَيْنِ وَقَرَّبَهُمَا وَأَخْلَعَ عَلَيْهِمَا وَقَالَ لَهُمَا أَنْتُمْ فِي مَرْتَبَةِ أَبِيكُمْ فَلَا تُكَدِّرْ وَاخَوَاطِرَكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa anna wālidahum māta fa-ḥazina ʿalayhi al-sulṭānu wa-aqbala ʿalā al-waladayni wa-qarrabahumā wa-akhlaʿa ʿalayhimā wa-qāla lahumā antum fī martabati abīkum fa-lā tukaddir wā-khawāṭirakum
sentences.l: So it-happened that their-father died; so the-sultan grieved over-him, and turned toward the-two-sons, and drew-them-near, and bestowed-a-robe upon-them, and said to-them: "You are in the-rank of-your-father, so do-not trouble your-minds."
sentences.i: It happened that their father died. The sultan grieved for him, turned to the two sons, drew them near and bestowed robes of honour on them, saying, "You stand in your father's place, so do not let your hearts be troubled."
sentences.n: واخواطركم: the plural ending of the verb (تكدروا "do (you all) trouble") is printed on the next word, so the print reads تكدر واخواطركم. It is vowelled as printed; read tukaddirū khawāṭirakum. وأخلع is form IV where Classical has خَلَعَ عَلَى "bestow a robe of honour on". أنتم "you" (pl.) is used to the two brothers.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحُوا وَقَبَّلُوا الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَعَمِلُوا الْعَزَا لِأَبِيهِمْ إِلَى إِتْمَامِ شَهْرٍ ثُمَّ دَخَلُوا فِى الْوِزَارَةِ وَصَارَ الْحُكْمُ بِأَيْدِيهِمَا كَمَا كَانَ بِيَدِ أَبِيهِمَا
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥū wa-qabbalū al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-ʿamilū al-ʿazā li-abīhim ilā itmāmi shahrin thumma dakhalū fī al-wizārati wa-ṣāra al-ḥukmu bi-aydīhimā kamā kāna bi-yadi abīhimā
sentences.l: So they-rejoiced, and kissed the-ground between his-hands, and made the-mourning for-their-father until the-completion of-a-month; then they-entered into the-vizierate, and the-rule became in-their-two-hands, as it-was in the-hand of-their-father.
sentences.i: They rejoiced and kissed the ground before him, and kept the mourning for their father until a month was complete. Then they entered the vizierate, and the government passed into their hands as it had been in their father's.
sentences.n: Kissing the ground before a ruler is the formal gesture of thanks. The plural verbs (فرحوا ... دخلوا) cover the two brothers together.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ إِذَا أَرَادَ السُّلْطَانُ السَّفَرَ يُسَافِرُ وَاحِدٌ مِنْهُمَا
sentences.tr: wa-kāna idhā arāda al-sulṭānu al-safara yusāfiru wāḥidun minhumā
sentences.l: And it-was, when the-sultan wanted the-travel, travelled one of-the-two.
sentences.i: Whenever the sultan wished to travel, one of the two would travel with him.

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقَ فِي لَيْلَةٍ مِنَ اللَّيَالِي وَكَانَتْ سَفَرُالْكَبِيرِ مَعَ السُّلْطَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqa fī laylatin mina al-layālī wa-kānat safaru al-kabīri maʿa al-sulṭāni
sentences.l: So it-happened, on a-night of the-nights, and was-feminine the-travel of-the-elder with the-sultan.
sentences.i: It happened one night, when it was the elder's turn to travel with the sultan,
sentences.n: كانت is feminine though سفر is masculine in form; the sense is the elder's "turn" or "journey" (a feminine noun like سفرة). سفرالكبير is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ يَتَحَدَّثُونَ إِذْ قَالَ الْكَبِيرُ لِلصَّغِيرِ يَا أَخِي قَصْدِي أَنْ أَتَزَوَّجَ أَنَا وَأَنْتَ فِي لَيْلَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hum yataḥaddathūna idh qāla al-kabīru li-al-ṣaghīri yā akhī qaṣdī an atazawwaja anā wa-anta fī laylatin wāḥidatin
sentences.l: So while they conversing, behold said the-elder to-the-younger: "O my-brother, my-intent that I-marry, I and-you, in one night."
sentences.i: While they were talking together, the elder said to the younger, "My brother, I intend that you and I should marry on one and the same night."
sentences.n: The two brothers were talking, with the elder in the sultan's party. أَنْ أَتَزَوَّجَ أَنَا وَأَنْتَ "that I marry, I and you" uses the full pronoun to join the two of them.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الصَّغِيرُ اِفْعَلْ يَا أَخِي مَا تُرِيدُ فَإِنِّي مُوَافِقُكَ عَلَى مَاتَقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-ṣaghīru ifʿal yā akhī mā turīdu fa-innī muwāfiquka ʿalā mā taqūlu
sentences.l: So said the-younger: "Do, O my-brother, what you-want, for-indeed-I agreeing-with-you in what you-say."
sentences.i: The younger said, "Do as you wish, my brother, for I agree with whatever you say."

sentences.t: فَاتَّفَقُوا عَلَى ذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-ittafaqū ʿalā dhālika
sentences.l: So they-agreed upon that.
sentences.i: So they agreed on it.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْكَبِيرَ قَالَ لِأَخِيهِ إِنْ قَدَّرَاللَّهُ وَخَطَبْنَا بِنْتَيْنِ وَدَخَلْنَا فِي لَيْلَةٍ وَاحِدَةٍ وَوَضَعَتَا فِي يَوْمٍ وَاحِدٍ وَأَرَادَ اللَّهُ وَجَاءَتْ زَوْجَتُكَ بِصَبِيٍّ وَجَاءَتْ زَوْجَتِي بِبِنْتٍ نُزَوِّجُهُمَا لِبَعْضِهِمَا وَيَصِيرَا أَوْلَادَ عَمٍّ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-kabīra qāla li-akhīhi in qaddara Allāhu wa-khaṭabnā bintayni wa-dakhalnā fī laylatin wāḥidatin wa-waḍaʿatā fī yawmin wāḥidin wa-arāda Allāhu wa-jāʾat zawjatuka bi-ṣabiyyin wa-jāʾat zawjatī bi-bintin nuzawwijuhumā li-baʿḍihimā wa-yaṣīrā awlāda ʿammin
sentences.l: Then indeed the-elder said to-his-brother: "If God decree, and we-ask-for-the-hand-of two-daughters, and enter in one night, and they-two-give-birth on one day, and God will, and your-wife comes with-a-boy and my-wife comes with-a-girl, we-marry-them to-each-other, and they-become sons-of-an-uncle."
sentences.i: Then the elder said to his brother, "If God decrees it, and we ask for two girls in marriage and go in to them on one night, and they give birth on one day, and God wills that your wife bring a boy and mine a girl, we shall marry them to each other, and they will be cousins."
sentences.n: A long conditional chain: إن قدر الله ... وخطبنا ... ودخلنا ... ووضعتا ... وأراد الله ... وجاءت ... and only then the result, نزوجهما. قدرالله is printed as one word (read qaddara Allāhu). دخلنا "we went in" is the idiom for consummating a marriage; ووضعتا is the dual feminine "they (two women) gave birth". The result clause is introduced without فَـ, and ويصيرا is a dual verb without final ن, as if jussive.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نُورُالدِّينِ يَا أَخِي مَا تَأْخُذُ مِنْ وَلَدِي فِي مَهْرِ بِنْتِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Nūru al-Dīni yā akhī mā taʾkhudhu min waladī fī mahri bintika
sentences.l: So said Nūr al-Dīn: "O my-brother, what will-you-take from my-son as-the-dowry of-your-daughter?"
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn said, "My brother, what will you take from my son as the dowry for your daughter?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ آخُذُ مِنْ وَلَدِكَ لِبِنْتِي ثَلٰثَةَ آلَافِ دِينَارٍ وَثَلٰثَ سَاتِينَ وَثَلٰثَ ضِيَاعٍ وَإِنْ كَتَبَ الشَّابُّ بِغَيْرِ هَذَا لَا يَصِحُّ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla ākhudhu min waladika li-bintī thalāthata ālāfi dīnārin wa-thalātha sātīna wa-thalātha ḍiyāʿin wa-in kataba al-shābbu bi-ghayri hādhā lā yaṣiḥḥu
sentences.l: So he-said: "I-take from your-son, for-my-daughter, three thousands of-dinars, and three gardens, and three estates; and if the-youth writes with-other-than this, not it-is-valid."
sentences.i: He said, "For my daughter I shall take from your son three thousand dinars, three gardens and three estates; and if the young man writes the contract on any other terms, it is not valid."
sentences.n: ساتين is evidently بساتين "gardens" with the first letter dropped in print; it is vowelled as printed. ثلث is ثَلَاثَ "three" before a plural (ثلثة is the usual defective spelling, with the dagger alif). كتب is "writes" (the marriage contract).

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ نُورُالدِّينِ هَذَا الْكَلَامَ قَالَ مَا هَذَا الْمَهْرُ بِالشَّرْطِ عَلَى وَلَدِي
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Nūru al-Dīni hādhā al-kalāma qāla mā hādhā al-mahru bi-al-sharṭi ʿalā waladī
sentences.l: So when Nūr al-Dīn heard this the-speech, he-said: "What is this the-dowry, with-the-condition upon my-son?
sentences.i: When Nūr al-Dīn heard these words he said, "What is this dowry, laid as a condition upon my son?
sentences.n: بالشرط: the بِـ is "by means of, under": a dowry fixed as a stipulated condition.

sentences.t: أَمَا تَعْلَمُ أَنَّنَا إِخْوَةٌ وَنَحْنُ الِاثْنَانِ بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ وُزَرَاءُ وَنَحْنُ فِي مَقَامٍ وَاحِدٍ
sentences.tr: amā taʿlamu annanā ikhwatun wa-naḥnu al-ithnāni bi-faḍli Allāhi wuzarāʾu wa-naḥnu fī maqāmin wāḥidin
sentences.l: Do-you-not know that-we brothers, and-we, the-two, by the-favour of-God, viziers, and-we in one station?
sentences.i: Do you not know that we are brothers, that by God's favour we two are both viziers, and that we stand in one and the same station?

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْوَاجِبُ عَلَيْكَ أَنْ تُقَدِّمَ ابْنَتَكَ لِوَلَدِي مِنْ غَيْرِ مَهْرٍ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-wājibu ʿalayka an tuqaddima ibnataka li-waladī min ghayri mahrin
sentences.l: And was the-obligatory upon-you that you-present your-daughter to-my-son from other-than dowry.
sentences.i: It was your duty to offer your daughter to my son without any dowry,

sentences.t: وَإِنْ كَانَ لَابُدَّ مِنْ مَهْرٍ فَتَجْعَلُ شَيْئًا مَعْلُومًا لِيَظْهَرَ لِلنَّاسِ
sentences.tr: wa-in kāna lā budda min mahrin fa-tajʿalu shayʾan maʿlūman li-yaẓhara li-al-nāsi
sentences.l: And if there-was no-escape from a-dowry, then you-make a-thing known, so-that it-appear to-the-people.
sentences.i: or if a dowry cannot be avoided, then fix some stated sum, so that it is plain to people.
sentences.n: فتجعل is an indicative verb after فَـ used as a command ("then you make"); Classical would have the imperative فَاجْعَلْ.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّكَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ الذَّكَرَ أَفْضَلُ مِنَ الْأُنْثَى وَوَلَدِي ذَكَرٌ وَنُذْكَرُبِهِ بِخِلَافِ ابْنَتِكَ
sentences.tr: fa-innaka taʿlamu anna al-dhakara afḍalu mina al-unthā wa-waladī dhakarun wa-nudhkaru bihi bi-khilāfi ibnatika
sentences.l: For-indeed-you know that the-male is better than the-female, and-my-son a-male, and-we-are-mentioned by-him, in-contrast-to your-daughter.
sentences.i: For you know that the male is better than the female; my son is a male, and through him we are remembered, unlike your daughter.
sentences.n: ونذكربه is printed as one word: وَنُذْكَرُ بِهِ, passive, "we are mentioned, held in remembrance, through him". A family is remembered by its sons.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ وَمَالَهَا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla wa-mā lahā
sentences.l: So he-said: "And-what to-her?"
sentences.i: He said, "And what is wrong with her?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَا نُذْكَرُبِهَا بَيْنَ الْأُمَرَاءِ وَلَكِنْ أَنْتَ تُرِيدُانْ تَفْعَلَ مَعِي كَمَا فَعَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lā nudhkaru bihā bayna al-umarāʾi wa-lākin anta turīdu an tafʿala maʿī ka-mā faʿala baʿḍuhum
sentences.l: So he-said: "We-are-not-mentioned by-her among the-emirs; but you, you-want to-do with me as did some-of-them.
sentences.i: He said, "We are not remembered through her among the emirs. But you want to deal with me as one man did with another.
sentences.n: تريدان is printed as one word: تُرِيدُ أَنْ "you want to", read turīdu an, the same kind of run-together as أمران above. ما فعل بعضهم "as some of them did" introduces the anecdote that follows.

sentences.t: قِيلَ إِنَّ بَعْضَ النَّاسِ تَدَّمَ عَلَى بَعْضِ أَصْحَابِهِ فَقَصَدَهُ فِي حَاجَةٍ فَقَالَ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ نَقْضِي حَاجَتَكَ وَلَكِنْ غَدًا
sentences.tr: qīla inna baʿḍa al-nāsi taddama ʿalā baʿḍi aṣḥābihi fa-qaṣadahu fī ḥājatin fa-qāla bi-smi Allāhi naqḍī ḥājataka wa-lākin ghadan
sentences.l: It-was-said that some of-the-people approached some-of his-companions, and-he-sought-him out for a-need; so he-said: "In-the-name of-God, we-will-fulfil your-need, but tomorrow."
sentences.i: It is told that a man went to one of his friends and asked him for a favour; and the friend said, "In God's name, we will grant your request, but tomorrow."
sentences.n: تدم is evidently تَقَدَّمَ "he came forward to, approached" with the ق dropped in print. It is vowelled as the shortened form with a shadda (taddama), which keeps the printed letters. The sense, as the verse below confirms, is of a petitioner and a put-off.

sentences.t: فَأَنْشَدَ فِي الْجَوَابِ شِعْرًا
sentences.tr: fa-anshada fī al-jawābi shiʿran
sentences.l: So he-recited in the-reply poetry.
sentences.i: and the other answered in verse:

sentences.t: اِذَا كَانَ فِى الْحَاجَاتِ مَهْلًا اِلَى غَدٍ * فَذَاكَ يَكُونُ طَرْدًا لِمَنْ كَانَ عَارِفًا
sentences.tr: idhā kāna fī al-ḥājāti mahlan ilā ghadin * fa-dhāka yakūnu ṭardan li-man kāna ʿārifan
sentences.l: If there-be, in needs, a-delay till tomorrow, * then that is a-driving-away of-one who-was an-acquaintance.
sentences.i: If, where needs are concerned, there is delay until tomorrow, that is a rebuff to one who was a friend.
sentences.n: Verse, copied as printed with the edition's own pointing. The verse is the put-off man's reply; عَارِفًا is "one who knows", hence an acquaintance or friend.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ شَمْسُ الدِّينِ أَرَاكَ تُقَصِّرُ وَتَعْمَلُ بِنْتَكَ أَفْضَلَ مِنِ ابْنِي
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu Shams al-Dīn arāka tuqaṣṣiru wa-taʿmalu bintaka afḍala min ibnī
sentences.l: And he-said to-him, Shams al-Dīn: "I-see-you you-fall-short, and you-make your-daughter better than my-son."
sentences.i: Then Shams al-Dīn said to him, "I see that you fall short, and that you rate your daughter above my son."
sentences.n: Shams al-Dīn is the elder brother, the father of the bride. بِنْتَكَ ("your daughter") is vocalised as printed, but the next speeches show that the two children in question are Shams al-Dīn's daughter and Nūr al-Dīn's son (بِنْتِي لِوَلَدِكَ), so one would expect "your son ... my daughter" here; the printed text may be slipped. تُقَصِّرُ is "you fall short" (of what is due).

sentences.t: لَاشَكَّ أَنَّكَ نَاقِصُ عَقْلٍ وَلَالَكَ أَخْلَاقٌ تَذْكُرُ شِرْكَةَ الْوِزَارَةِ
sentences.tr: lāshakka annaka nāqiṣu ʿaqlin wa-lā-laka akhlāqun tadhkuru shirkata al-wizārati
sentences.l: No-doubt that-you deficient of-intellect, and not-to-you manners: you-mention partnership-of the-vizierate.
sentences.i: Without doubt you are short of wit, and you have no manners, that you speak of a partnership in the vizierate.
sentences.n: وَلَالَكَ is printed as one word: wa + lā + li-ka, the لِـ being the possessive "to" ("not to you manners" = "you have no manners"). Here the sense of أَخْلَاقٌ is good manners, good character.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا مَا أَدْخَلْتُكَ مَعِي فِى الْوِزَارَةِ إِلَّا شَفَقَةً عَلَيْكَ وَتَبْقَى تُسَاعِدُنِي وَنَكُونُ لِي مُعِينًا وَلَا أَكْسِرُ بِخَاطِرِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-anā mā adkhaltuka maʿī fī al-wizārati illā shafaqatan ʿalayka wa-tabqā tusāʿiduni wa-nakūnu lī muʿīnan wa-lā aksiru bi-khāṭirika
sentences.l: And I, not I-brought-you-in with-me in the vizierate except pity upon-you, and you-remain you-help-me, and we-are to-me a-helper, and not I-break in-your-heart.
sentences.i: As for me, I brought you into the vizierate beside me only out of pity for you, that you might stay and help me and be a support to me, and so as not to wound your feelings.
sentences.n: وَنَكُونُ is printed with "we" where the sense wants "you will be"; it is vocalised as printed. وَلَا أَكْسِرُ بِخَاطِرِكَ, "and I do not break in your heart", is an idiom for not hurting someone's feelings; the verb takes بِـ.

sentences.t: وَحَيْثُمَا هَذَا الْقَوْلُ قَوْلُكَ وَاللَّهِ لَا أُزَوِّجُ بِنْتِي لِوَلَدِكَ وَلَوْ وَزَنْتَ ثِقْلَهَا ذَهَبًا
sentences.tr: wa-ḥaythumā hādhā al-qawlu qawluka wa-Allāhi lā uzawwiju bintī li-waladika wa-law wazanta thiqlahā dhahaban
sentences.l: And wherever this the-saying your-saying, by-God not I-marry my-daughter to-your-son, and-if you-weighed her-weight gold.
sentences.i: Since that is what you say, by God I will not marry my daughter to your son, even if you were to weigh out her weight in gold.
sentences.n: حَيْثُمَا is used here in the Middle Arabic sense "since, seeing that", not Classical "wherever".

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ نُورُالدِّينِ كَلَامَ أَخِيهِ اغْتَاظَ وَقَالَ وَأَنَا مَا بَقِيتُ أُزَوِّجُ ابْنِي ابْنَتَكَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Nūr al-Dīn kalāma akhīhi ightāẓa wa-qāla wa-anā mā baqītu uzawwiju ibnī ibnataka
sentences.l: And when heard Nūr al-Dīn the-speech-of his-brother, he-was-enraged, and said: "And I, not I-remained I-marry my-son your-daughter."
sentences.i: When Nūr al-Dīn heard his brother's words he was enraged, and he said, "And I, for my part, will no longer marry my son to your daughter."
sentences.n: مَا بَقِيتُ followed by a present verb means "I no longer ..." (literally "I have not remained ...-ing"). The verb أُزَوِّجُ takes two objects: the person given in marriage (ابْنِي) and the bride (ابْنَتَكَ), without a preposition. نُورُالدِّينِ is printed as one word here.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَمْسُ الدِّينِ أَنَا لَا أَرْضَاءَ لَهَا بَعْلًا
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Shams al-Dīn anā lā arḍāʾa lahā baʿlan
sentences.l: So he-said, Shams al-Dīn: "I, not I-accept for-her a-husband."
sentences.i: Shams al-Dīn said, "For my part, I will not accept him as a husband for her."
sentences.n: أَرْضَاءَ is obscure as printed: the ء is probably a misprint for ه, i.e. أَرْضَاهُ "I accept him" (arḍāhu), or else a slip for أَرْضَى "I accept". It is vocalised as printed and translated by the likely sense. بَعْلًا, "husband", is accusative of state.

sentences.t: وَلَوْلَا إِنِّي فِى السَّفَرِ لَكُنْتُ عَمِلْتُ مَعَكَ الْعِبَرَ
sentences.tr: wa-lawlā innī fī al-safari la-kuntu ʿamiltu maʿaka al-ʿibara
sentences.l: And were-it-not that-I in the-journey, I-would-have I-did with-you the-lessons.
sentences.i: Were I not on the point of departure, I would make an example of you.
sentences.n: لَوْلَا إِنِّي فِي السَّفَرِ is "if it were not that I am about to travel". The result clause لَكُنْتُ عَمِلْتُ (kuntu + perfect) is a Middle Arabic way of saying "I would have done". الْعِبَرَ (plural of عِبْرَة) are warnings, object lessons: "to do the lessons with you" is to make an example of someone.

sentences.t: وَلَكِنْ لَمَّا أَرْجِعُ مِنْ سَفَرِي فَرَجٌ أُرِيكَ مَاتَقْتَضِي مُرُوَّتِي
sentences.tr: wa-lākin lammā arjiʿu min safarī farajun urīka mā taqtaḍī muruwwatī
sentences.l: But when I-return from my-journey, relief: I-show-you what requires my-manliness.
sentences.i: But when I return from my journey, there will be satisfaction; I shall show you what my honour demands.
sentences.n: فَرَجٌ is obscure here: literally "relief", perhaps meaning "then comes the relief (of settling this)"; it may be corrupt. لَمَّا أَرْجِعُ has a present verb after لَمَّا, which is Middle Arabic. مُرُوَّتِي is printed without hamza, so it is vocalised muruwwa (not Classical مُرُوءَة): manliness, honour, a sense of what is due to one's standing. مَاتَقْتَضِي is printed as one word.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ نُورُالدِّينِ مِنْ أَخِيهِ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ امْتَلَأَ غَيْظًا وَغَابَ عَنِ الدُّنْيَا وَكَتَمَ مَا بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Nūr al-Dīn min akhīhi dhālika al-kalāma imtalaʾa ghayẓan wa-ghāba ʿan al-dunyā wa-katama mā bihi
sentences.l: And when heard Nūr al-Dīn from his-brother that the-speech, he-was-filled with-rage, and was-absent from the-world, and concealed what was-in-him.
sentences.i: When Nūr al-Dīn heard those words from his brother he was filled with rage; the world went dark to him, and he hid what he felt.
sentences.n: غَابَ عَنِ الدُّنْيَا, "he was absent from the world", means he lost awareness of everything around him. مَا بِهِ, "what is in him", is what he was suffering. غَيْظًا is accusative of specification, "full in respect of rage".

sentences.t: وَبَاتَ كُلُّ وَاحِدٍ فِي نَاحِيَةٍ
sentences.tr: wa-bāta kullu wāḥidin fī nāḥiyatin
sentences.l: And spent-the-night each one in a-side.
sentences.i: And each of them spent the night in a part of the house by himself.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ بَرَزَ السُّلْطَانُ لِلسَّفَرِ وَغَدَا فِى الْجِيزَةِ وَقَصَدَ الْأَهْرَامَ وَصَحِبَهُ الْوَزِيرُ شَمْسُ الدِّينِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu baraza al-sulṭānu li-al-safari wa-ghadā fī al-Jīzati wa-qaṣada al-ahrāma wa-ṣaḥibahu al-wazīru Shams al-Dīn
sentences.l: And when the-morning became-morning, the-sultan came-forth for-the-journey, and set-out-early to al-Jīza, and made-for the-pyramids, and accompanied-him the-vizier Shams al-Dīn.
sentences.i: When morning came, the sultan rode out for his journey. He set out at daybreak for Giza and made for the pyramids, and the vizier Shams al-Dīn went with him.
sentences.n: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ, "when the morning became morning", is the stock dawn formula. الْجِيزَةِ is Giza, across the Nile from Cairo, and الْأَهْرَامَ the pyramids.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ أَخِيهِ نُورِ الدِّينِ فَبَاتَ تِلْكَ اللَّيْلَةَ فِي أَشَدِّ مَا يَكُونُ مِنَ الْغَيْظِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri akhīhi Nūr al-Dīn fa-bāta tilka al-laylata fī ashaddi mā yakūnu mina al-ghayẓi
sentences.l: And as-for what was of the-affair-of his-brother Nūr al-Dīn: he-spent-the-night that the-night in the-most-intense of-what is from the-rage.
sentences.i: As for what became of his brother Nūr al-Dīn, he passed that night in the extremity of rage.
sentences.n: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ ... فَ is the storyteller's formula for turning to another character: "as for what happened with X, ..."; the فَـ opens the main clause.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ قَامَ وَصَلَّى الصُّبْحَ وَعَمَدَ إِلَى خِزَانَتِهِ وَأَخَذَ مِنْهَا خُرْجًا صَغِيرًا وَمَلَأَهُ ذَهَبًا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu qāma wa-ṣallā al-ṣubḥa wa-ʿamada ilā khizānatihi wa-akhadha minhā khurjan ṣaghīran wa-malaʾahu dhahaban
sentences.l: And when the-morning became-morning, he-rose, and prayed the-dawn, and made-for his-treasury, and took from-it a-saddlebag small, and filled-it gold.
sentences.i: When morning came he rose and said the dawn prayer, then went to his strongroom and took out a small saddlebag and filled it with gold.
sentences.n: خُرْجًا is a saddlebag, two pouches joined to hang over a mount's back. صَلَّى الصُّبْحَ is "he prayed the dawn (prayer)".

sentences.t: وَتَذَكَّرَ قَوْلَ أَخِيهِ وَحَقَارَتَهُ عِنْدَهُ فَأَنْشَدَ وَجَعَلَ يَقُولُ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: wa-tadhakkara qawla akhīhi wa-ḥaqāratahu ʿindahu fa-anshada wa-jaʿala yaqūlu hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: And he-remembered the-saying-of his-brother and his-contempt with-him, and recited, and began he-says these the-verses.
sentences.i: He remembered his brother's words and the contempt in which his brother held him, and he recited, saying these verses:
sentences.n: وَحَقَارَتَهُ عِنْدَهُ is "and his [Shams al-Dīn's] belittling, in his [Shams al-Dīn's] view": the contempt is the brother's. جَعَلَ يَقُولُ ("he began to say") is the usual inchoative construction.

sentences.t:
سَافِرْ تَجِدْ عِوَضًا عَمَّنْ تُفَارِقُهُ * وَانْصَبْ فَانَّ لَذِيذَ الْعَيْشِ فِي النَّصَبِ
مَا فِي الْمَقَرَارَى عِزًّا وَلَا اَرَبًا * سِوَى الْعَنَا فَدَعِ الْاَوْطَانَ وَاغْتَرِبِ
sentences.tr:
sāfir tajid ʿiwaḍan ʿamman tufāriquhu * wa-anṣab fa-inna ladhīdha al-ʿayshi fī al-naṣabi
mā fī al-maqarārā ʿizzan wa-lā arabā * siwā al-ʿanā fa-daʿi al-awṭāna wa-ightaribi
sentences.l:
Travel, you-will-find a-substitute for-whom you-part-from * and toil, for the-sweet-of the-life is in the-toil.
Not in the-staying-place honour nor need * except the-hardship, so leave the-homelands and go-abroad.
sentences.i: Travel, and you will find a replacement for whoever you leave behind; and labour, for the sweetness of life lies in labour. * There is no honour or gain in staying put, only hardship, so leave your homelands and go into exile.
sentences.n: The print points this verse; it is copied as printed. الْمَقَرَارَى is obscure and possibly corrupt: it looks like a form of مَقَرّ, "place of staying" (the sense must be "staying at home"). عِزًّا is accusative after مَا as printed. The poem rhymes on -bi.

sentences.t:
اِنِّي رَايْتُ وُقُوفَ الْمَاءِ يُفْسِدُهُ * اِنْ سَاحَ طَابَ وَاِنْ لَمْ يَجْرِ لَمْ يَطِبِ
وَالْبَدْرُ لَوْلَا اُفُولٌ مِنْهُ مَانَظَرَتْ * اِلَيْهِ فِي كُلِّ حِينٍ عَيْنُ مُرْتَقِبِ
sentences.tr:
innī raʾaytu wuqūfa al-māʾi yufsiduhu * in sāḥa ṭāba wa-in lam yajri lam yaṭibi
wa-al-badru law-lā ufūlun minhu mā naẓarat * ilayhi fī kulli ḥīnin ʿaynu murtaqibi
sentences.l:
Indeed I saw the-standing-still of-the-water spoils-it * if it-flowed it-was-good, and if not it-ran it-was-not-good.
And the-full-moon, were-it-not for-a-setting from-it, not looked * at-it in every time the-eye-of a-watcher.
sentences.i: I have seen that standing still spoils water: if it flows it is sweet, and if it does not run it is not. * And the full moon, were it not for its setting, no watcher's eye would look on it at every hour.
sentences.n: Printed pointing kept. رَايْتُ is printed with bare alif, read raʾaytu. مَانَظَرَتْ is one word, mā naẓarat.

sentences.t: وَالْاُسْدُ لَوْلَا فِرَاقُ الْغَابِ مَا اقْتَنَصَتْ * وَالسَّهْمُ لَوْلَا فِرَاقُ الْقَوْسِ لَمْ يُصِبِ
sentences.tr: wa-al-usdu law-lā firāqu al-ghābi mā iqtanaṣat * wa-al-sahmu law-lā firāqu al-qawsi lam yuṣibi
sentences.l: And the-lions, were-it-not for-the-parting-from the-thicket, not hunted * and the-arrow, were-it-not for-the-parting-from the-bow, not hit.
sentences.i: The lions, but for leaving the thicket, would never hunt; and the arrow, but for leaving the bow, would never strike.
sentences.n: Printed pointing kept. الْاُسْدُ is the plural of أَسَد, lion, pointed as printed.

sentences.t:
وَالتِّبْرُ كَالتُّرْبِ مُلْقًى فِي مَعَادِنِهِ * وَالْعُودُ فِي اَرْضِهِ نَوْعٌ مِنَ الْحَطَبِ
فَانْ تَغَرَّبَ هَذَا عَزَّ مَطْلَبُهُ * وَاِنْ تَغَرَّبَ هَذَا زَادَ فِي الذَّهَبِ
sentences.tr:
wa-al-tibru ka-al-turbi mulqan fī maʿādinihi * wa-al-ʿūdu fī arḍihi nawʿun mina al-ḥaṭabi
fa-in tagharraba hādhā ʿazza maṭlabuhu * wa-in tagharraba hādhā zāda fī al-dhahabi
sentences.l:
And the-gold-dust like-the-dust cast-down in its-mines * and the-aloe-wood in its-land a-kind of the-firewood.
So if goes-abroad this, dear-is its-seeking * and if goes-abroad this, it-increased in the-gold.
sentences.i: Gold-dust lies like common dirt, cast about in its mines, and aloe-wood in its own land is one kind of firewood. * But if the one goes abroad, it becomes costly to seek; and if the other goes abroad, it rises to the price of gold.
sentences.n: Printed pointing kept. هَذَا appears twice, once for each of the two things just named: first the gold, then the aloe-wood (the second clause, "it increased in the gold", is the more natural fit for the wood, and for the first, "dear is its seeking"). The couplet's sense is clear but the grammar is loose. الْعُودُ is aloe-wood, the costly incense wood.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ مِنْ شِعْرِهِ أَمَرَ بَعْضَ غِلْمَانِهِ أَنْ يَشُدَّ لَهُ بَغْلَةَ النُّوبَةِ بِسَرْجِهَا الْمُضَرَّبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha min shiʿrihi amara baʿḍa ghilmānihi an yashudda lahu baghlata al-nūbati bi-sarjihā al-muḍarrabi
sentences.l: So-when he-finished from his-poetry, he-commanded some-of his-lads that they-saddle for-him the-mule of-Nubia with-its-saddle the-quilted.
sentences.i: When he had finished his poem, he ordered one of his young men to saddle for him the Nubian mule, with its quilted saddle.
sentences.n: شعره is read shiʿr, "poetry", since he has just been reciting; with a different vowel (shaʿr) it would be "hair". The Arabic says "the mule of Nubia", a Nubian mule; the saddle is "quilted" (muḍarrab), padded with stitching.

sentences.t: وَهِيَ بَغْلَةٌ زُرْ زُورِيَّةٌ عَالِيَةُ الظَّهْرِ كَأَنَّهَا قُبَّةٌ مَبْنِيَّةٌ
sentences.tr: wa-hiya baghlatun zur zūriyyatun ʿāliyatu al-ẓahri ka-annahā qubbatun mabniyyatun
sentences.l: And-she a-mule starling-ish, high-of the-back, as-if-she a-dome built.
sentences.i: She was a starling-grey mule, tall in the back, as though she were a domed building.
sentences.n: The edition prints زر زورية as two words; it is most likely one word, zurzūriyya, "starling-coloured" (zurzūr is the starling), so a dark speckled grey. It is kept as printed, and read as one adjective.

sentences.t: سَرْجُهَا ذَهَبٌ وَرِكَابَاتُهَا هِنْدِيَّةٌ عَلَيْهَا عَبَاءَةٌ كِسْرَوِيَّةٌ وَهِيَ كَأَنَّهَا عَرُوسَةٌ مُجَلَّيَةٌ
sentences.tr: sarjuhā dhahabun wa-rikābātuhā hindiyyatun ʿalayhā ʿabāʾatun kisrawiyyatun wa-hiya ka-annahā ʿarūsatun mujallayatun
sentences.l: Its-saddle gold, and-its-stirrups Indian; upon-it a-cloak Khosrow-ish; and-she as-if-she a-bride adorned.
sentences.i: Its saddle was gold and its stirrups Indian; over it lay a cloak fit for a Chosroes, and she looked like a bride adorned for display.
sentences.n: كسروية means "of Kisrā", the Sasanian king Khosrow (Chosroes), the byword for royal splendour. مجلية is read mujallayah, "displayed, adorned" (a bride is "unveiled" to her groom); the form is obscure and may stand for the classical مُجَلَّاةٌ.

sentences.t: وَأَمَرَهُ أَنْ يَجْعَلَ عَلَيْهَا بِسَاطًا حَرِيرًا وَسَجَّادَةً وَجَعَلَ الْخُرْجَ مِنْ تَحْتِ السَّجَّادَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-amarahu an yajʿala ʿalayhā bisāṭan ḥarīran wa-sajjādatan wa-jaʿala al-khurja min taḥti al-sajjādati
sentences.l: And-he-commanded-him that he-put upon-her a-carpet silken and-a-rug, and-he-put the-saddlebag from beneath the-rug.
sentences.i: He told him to lay over her a silk carpet and a rug, and the saddlebag was placed beneath the rug.
sentences.n: The last verb has no stated subject; it is the servant carrying out the order, so the sense is "and he placed".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لِلْغُلَامِ وَالْعَبِيدِ قَصْدِي أَتَفَرَّجُ خَارِجَ الْمَدِينَةِ وَأَرُوحُ نَوَاحِيَ الْقَلْيُوبِيَّةِ وَأَبَاتُ ثَلَٰثَ لَيَالٍ فَلَا أَحَدَ مِنْكُمْ يَتْبَعُنِي
sentences.tr: thumma qāla li-al-ghulāmi wa-al-ʿabīdi qaṣdī ataffarraju khārija al-madīnati wa-arūḥu nawāḥiya al-qalyūbiyyati wa-abātu thalātha layālin fa-lā aḥada minkum yatbaʿunī
sentences.l: Then he-said to-the-lad and-the-slaves: My-intention (is) I-take-a-stroll outside the-city, and-I-go (to) the-districts of-Qalyubiyya, and-I-spend-the-night three nights; so-not anyone of-you follows-me.
sentences.i: Then he said to the lad and the servants, "I mean to go out for a stroll beyond the city, to wander the districts of al-Qalyubiyya and spend three nights away. Let none of you follow me,
sentences.n: Here the verbs of intent are in the plain imperfect (أَتَفَرَّجُ، أَرُوحُ، أَبَاتُ) with no أَنْ before them, and the prohibition is a statement, "so not anyone of you follows me" (يَتْبَعُنِي, not the classical jussive). This is ordinary Middle Arabic. أَرُوحُ takes a direct object ("I go to the districts"). ثلث is the edition's defective spelling of ثلاث, pointed with a dagger alif. القليوبية is the district north of Cairo.

sentences.t: فَإِنَّ عِنْدِي ضِيقَ صَدْرٍوَأَ سْرَعَ وَرَكِبَ الْبَغْلَةَ
sentences.tr: fa-inna ʿindī ḍīqa ṣadri-wa-a sraʿa wa-rakiba al-baghlata
sentences.l: For-indeed with-me (is) narrowness-of chest. And-he-hastened and-he-rode the-mule.
sentences.i: for my heart is heavy with distress." And he made haste and mounted the mule.
sentences.n: The edition prints صدروا سرع, with the word-space in the wrong place: it is ضيق صدر وأسرع, "narrowness of chest, and he hastened". The letters are kept as printed, so the word صَدْرٍوَأَ is three things run together (ṣadr, wa-, and the alif of أَسْرَعَ), and the next word سْرَعَ is the rest of the verb. "Narrowness of chest" is the idiom for being oppressed and out of spirits.

sentences.t: وَأَخَذَ مَعَهُ شَيْئًا قَلِيلًا مِنَ الزَّادِ وَخَرَجَ مِنْ مِصْرَ وَاسْتَقْبَلَ الْبَرَّ فَمَا جَاءَ عَلَيْهِ الظُّهْرُ حَتَّى دَخَلَ عَلَى مَدِينَةِ بِلْبِيسَ
sentences.tr: wa-akhadha maʿahu shayʾan qalīlan min al-zādi wa-kharaja min Miṣra wa-istaqbala al-barra fa-mā jāʾa ʿalayhi al-ẓuhru ḥattā dakhala ʿalā madīnati Bilbīsa
sentences.l: And-he-took with-him a-thing little of the-provision, and-he-went-out from Miṣr, and-he-faced the-open-country; and-not came upon-him the-noon until he-entered upon the-city of-Bilbays.
sentences.i: He took with him a little food, left Cairo, and set his face to the open country; noon had not yet come upon him when he reached the city of Bilbays.
sentences.n: مصر here is the city of Cairo (Miṣr), not the country. استقبل البر, "he faced the open land", means he struck out into the desert country.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَ عَنْ بَغْلَتِهِ وَاسْتَرَاحَ وَرَيَّحَ الْبَغْلَةَ وَأَخَذَ شَيْئًا مِنَ الزَّادِ فَأَكَلَهُ وَأَخَذَ مِنْ بِلْبِيسَ مَا يَأْكُلُهُ وَمَا يَعْلِفُهُ عَلَى بَغْلَتِهِ وَاسْتَقْبَلَ الْبَرَّ
sentences.tr: fa-nazala ʿan baghlatihi wa-istarāḥa wa-rayyaḥa al-baghlata wa-akhadha shayʾan min al-zādi fa-akalahu wa-akhadha min Bilbīsa mā yaʾkuluhu wa-mā yaʿlifuhu ʿalā baghlatihi wa-istaqbala al-barra
sentences.l: So-he-dismounted from his-mule, and-he-rested, and-he-gave-rest-to the-mule, and-he-took a-thing of the-provision and-he-ate-it, and-he-took from Bilbays what he-eats and-what he-feeds (as) fodder to his-mule, and-he-faced the-open-country.
sentences.i: He got down from his mule and rested, and let the mule rest; he took a little of his provisions and ate it, and bought in Bilbays what he needed to eat and fodder for his mule, and set his face to the open country again.
sentences.n: نزل عن, "descended from", is the usual way to say dismount.

sentences.t: فَمَا جَاءَ عَلَيْهِ اللَّيْلُ حَتَّى دَخَلَ بَلَدًا يُقَالُ لَهَا السَّعْدِيَهْ فَبَاتَ بِهَا وَأَخْرَجَ شَيْئًا أَكَلَهُ وَحَطَّ الْخُرْجَ تَحْتَ رَأْسِهِ وَفَرَشَ الْبِسَاطَ وَنَامَ فِي مَكَانِ الْبَرِّيَّةِ وَالْغَيْظُ غَالِبٌ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-mā jāʾa ʿalayhi al-laylu ḥattā dakhala baladan yuqālu lahā al-Saʿdiyah fa-bāta bihā wa-akhraja shayʾan akalahu wa-ḥaṭṭa al-khurja taḥta raʾsihi wa-farasha al-bisāṭa wa-nāma fī makāni al-barriyyati wa-al-ghayẓu ghālibun ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And-not came upon-him the-night until he-entered a-town it-is-said to-it al-Saʿdiyah; so-he-spent-the-night in-it, and-he-brought-out a-thing he-ate-it, and-he-set the-saddlebag beneath his-head, and-he-spread the-carpet, and-he-slept in a-place of-the-wilderness, and-the-rage overcoming upon-him.
sentences.i: Night had not yet fallen when he came to a town called al-Saʿdiyah, and he spent the night there. He took out something and ate it, put the saddlebag under his head, spread out the carpet and slept in a spot out in the wilderness, with rage still weighing on him.
sentences.n: The edition spells the name with final ه (السعديه), kept here with a sukūn on the hāʾ. شيئا أكله has no relative pronoun: "a thing (that) he ate".

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ بَاتَ فِي ذَٰلِكَ الْمَكَانِ فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ رَكِبَ وَسَارَ يَسُوقُ الْبَغْلَةَ إِلَى أَنْ وَصَلَ إِلَى مَدِينَةِ حَلَبَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu bāta fī dhālika al-makāni fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu rakiba wa-sāra yasūqu al-baghlata ilā an waṣala ilā madīnati Ḥalaba
sentences.l: Then indeed-he spent-the-night in that the-place; and-when the-morning became-morning, he-rode and-he-travelled driving the-mule until he-arrived at the-city of-Aleppo.
sentences.i: So he spent the night in that place, and when morning came he mounted and rode on, driving the mule, until he reached the city of Aleppo.
sentences.n: The route (Cairo, Bilbays, Aleppo, then Basra) is the storyteller's, and no distance is felt. أصبح الصباح, "the morning became morning", is a stock phrase for daybreak.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَ فِي بَعْضِ الْخَانَاتِ وَأَقَامَ ثَلَٰثَةَ أَيَّامٍ حَتَّى اسْتَرَاحَ وَرَيَّحَ الْبَغْلَةَ وَشَمَّ الْهَوَاءَ ثُمَّ عَزَمَ عَلَى السَّفَرِ وَرَكِبَ بَغْلَتَهُ وَخَرَجَ مُسَافِرًا لَا يَدْرِي أَيْنَ يَذْهَبُ
sentences.tr: fa-nazala fī baʿḍi al-khānāti wa-aqāma thalāthata ayyāmin ḥattā istarāḥa wa-rayyaḥa al-baghlata wa-shamma al-hawāʾa thumma ʿazama ʿalā al-safari wa-rakiba baghlatahu wa-kharaja musāfiran lā yadrī ayna yadhhabu
sentences.l: So-he-lodged in some-of the-khans and-he-stayed three days until he-rested and-he-rested the-mule and-he-smelled the-air; then he-resolved upon the-travel, and-he-rode his-mule and-he-went-out travelling, not knowing where he-goes.
sentences.i: He put up at one of the khans and stayed three days, until he and the mule were rested and he had taken the air. Then he resolved to travel on, mounted his mule and set out, not knowing where he was going.
sentences.n: شم الهواء, "smelled the air", means took the air, got some fresh air.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ سَائِرًا إِلَى أَنْ أَقْبَلَ عَلَى مَدِينَةِ الْبَصْرَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazal sāʾiran ilā an aqbala ʿalā madīnati al-Baṣrati
sentences.l: And-not he-ceased travelling until he-approached upon the-city of-al-Basra.
sentences.i: He kept on riding until he came to the city of Basra.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَشْعُرْ بِذَٰلِكَ حَتَّى نَزَلَ إِلَى الْخَانِ فَأَنْزَلَ الْخُرْجَ عَنِ الْبَغْلَةِ وَفَرَشَ السَّجَّادَةَ وَأَعْطَى الْبَغْلَةَ بِعُدَّتِهَا لِلْبَوَّابِ يُسَيِّرُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-lam yashʿur bi-dhālika ḥattā nazala ilā al-khāni fa-anzala al-khurja ʿani al-baghlati wa-farasha al-sajjādata wa-aʿṭā al-baghlata bi-ʿuddatihā li-al-bawwābi yusayyiruhā
sentences.l: And-not he-was-aware of-that until he-descended to the-khan; so-he-took-down the-saddlebag from the-mule, and-he-spread the-rug, and-he-gave the-mule with-its-gear to-the-doorkeeper (that) he-walk-her.
sentences.i: He was not aware of it until he had come down at the khan. There he took the saddlebag off the mule, spread the rug, and handed the mule over, with all her trappings, to the doorkeeper to walk her about.
sentences.n: The doorkeeper (bawwāb) of a khan looks after arriving animals. يسيرها is read yusayyiruhā, "make her walk", to cool her down; it follows the verb without أَنْ, as is usual in this text.

sentences.t: فَأَخَذَهَا وَسَيَّرَهَا فَاتَّفَقَ أَنَّ وَزِيرَ الْبَصْرَةِ جَالِسٌ فِي شُبَّاكِ قَصْرِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-akhadhahā wa-sayyarahā fa-ittafaqa anna wazīra al-Baṣrati jālisun fī shubbāki qaṣrihi
sentences.l: So-he-took-her and-he-walked-her; and-it-happened that the-vizier of-al-Basra (was) sitting in the-window of-his-palace.
sentences.i: He took her and walked her about, and it happened that the vizier of Basra was sitting at the window of his palace.
sentences.n: After أَنَّ the predicate is a plain nominative participle with no verb كان; the sense is past, "was sitting".

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ إِلَى الْبَغْلَةِ وَنَظَرَ مَا عَلَيْهَا مِنَ الْعُدَّةِ الْمُنَمَّةِ فَظَنَّهَا بَغْلَةَ مَوْكِبٍ وَمَرْكُوبَ وُزَرَاءَ أَوْ مُلُوكٍ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara ilā al-baghlati wa-naẓara mā ʿalayhā min al-ʿuddati al-munammati fa-ẓannahā baghlata mawkibin wa-markūba wuzarāʾa aw mulūkin
sentences.l: So-he-looked at the-mule, and-he-looked (at) what upon-her of the-gear the-adorned, and-he-supposed-her a-mule of-a-procession and-a-mount of-viziers or kings.
sentences.i: He looked at the mule, and at the ornate gear she carried, and took her for a mule of state processions, the mount of viziers or kings.
sentences.n: المنمة is obscure. It is read al-munammah, "adorned", perhaps standing for المنمقة (munammaqa, "embellished"); the reading is uncertain. موكب is a ceremonial procession.

sentences.t: فَتَفَكَّرَ فِي ذَٰلِكَ وَحَارَ عَقْلُهُ وَقَالَ لِبَعْضِ غِلْمَانِهِ ائْتِنِي بِهَٰذَا الْبَوَّابِ
sentences.tr: fa-tafakkara fī dhālika wa-ḥāra ʿaqluhu wa-qāla li-baʿḍi ghilmānihi ʾtinī bi-hādhā al-bawwābi
sentences.l: So-he-pondered in that, and-his-mind was-bewildered, and-he-said to-some-of his-lads: Bring-me this the-doorkeeper.
sentences.i: He pondered this, bewildered, and said to one of his young men, "Bring me that doorkeeper."
sentences.n: أتى بـ, "bring", takes its object with بِـ; the imperative ائتني is "come to me with", that is, "bring me".

sentences.t: فَذَهَبَ الْغُلَامُ وَأَتَى بِالْبَوَّابِ لِلْوَزِيرِ فَتَقَدَّمَ الْبَوَّابُ وَبَاسَ الْأَرْضَ
sentences.tr: fa-dhahaba al-ghulāmu wa-atā bi-al-bawwābi li-al-wazīri fa-taqaddama al-bawwābu wa-bāsa al-arḍa
sentences.l: So-he-went the-lad, and-he-brought the-doorkeeper to-the-vizier; so-he-advanced the-doorkeeper and-he-kissed the-ground.
sentences.i: The lad went and brought the doorkeeper to the vizier, and the doorkeeper stepped forward and kissed the ground.

sentences.t: وَكَانَ الْوَزِيرُ شَيْخًا كَبِيرًا فَقَالَ لِلْبَوَّابِ مَنْ يَكُنْ صَاحِبَ هَٰذِهِ الْبَغْلَةِ وَمَا صِفَاتُهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna al-wazīru shaykhan kabīran fa-qāla li-al-bawwābi man yakun ṣāḥiba hādhihi al-baghlati wa-mā ṣifātuhu
sentences.l: And-was the-vizier an-old-man great; so-he-said to-the-doorkeeper: Who is-he, (the) owner of-this the-mule, and-what (are) his-attributes?
sentences.i: The vizier was an aged man, and he said to the doorkeeper, "Who is the owner of this mule, and what is he like?"
sentences.n: مَنْ يَكُنْ is printed with the short, jussive-looking form of the verb, and صاحب is read as an accusative predicate; classically this would be مَنْ يَكُونُ صَاحِبُ. A loose Middle Arabic form: just read it as "who is". شيخا كبيرا, "a great old man", means very old.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ الْبَوَّابُ يَا سَيِّدِي صَاحِبُ هَٰذِهِ الْبَغْلَةِ شَابٌّ صَغِيرٌ ظَرِيفُ الشَّمَائِلِ عَلَيْهِ هَيْبَةٌ وَوَقَارٌ مِنْ أَوْلَادِ التُّجَّارِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla al-bawwābu yā sayyidī ṣāḥibu hādhihi al-baghlati shābbun ṣaghīrun ẓarīfu al-shamāʾili ʿalayhi haybatun wa-waqārun min awlādi al-tujjāri
sentences.l: So-he-said the-doorkeeper: O my-lord, the-owner of-this the-mule (is) a-young-man small, graceful-of the-traits; upon-him (is) awe and-dignity; (he is) of the-sons of-the-merchants.
sentences.i: The doorkeeper said, "My lord, the owner of this mule is a young man, graceful in his bearing, with an air of awe and dignity about him, one of the sons of merchants."
sentences.n: صغير here means young, not small in build.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَزِيرُ كَلَامَ الْبَوَّابِ قَامَ عَلَى حَيْلِهِ وَرَكِبَ وَسَارَ إِلَى الْخَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wazīru kalāma al-bawwābi qāma ʿalā ḥaylihi wa-rakiba wa-sāra ilā al-khāni
sentences.l: So-when he-heard the-vizier the-speech of-the-doorkeeper, he-rose upon his-strength, and-he-rode and-he-travelled to the-khan.
sentences.i: When the vizier heard the doorkeeper's words, he got up at once, mounted, and rode to the khan.
sentences.n: قام على حيله, "rose on his own strength", is read as an idiom for getting briskly to his feet; حيل is a colloquial form of ḥayl, "strength", and the reading is not certain.

sentences.t: وَدَخَلَ عَلَى الشَّابِّ فَلَمَّا رأَى نُورَالدِّينِ الْوَزِيرَ قَادِمٌ عَلَيْهِ قَامَ عَلَى حَيْلِهِ وَلَاقَاهُ وَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-dakhala ʿalā al-shābbi fa-lammā raʾā Nūr al-Dīni al-wazīra qādimun ʿalayhi qāma ʿalā ḥaylihi wa-lāqāhu wa-sallama ʿalayhi
sentences.l: And he-entered upon the youth; and when Nūr al-Dīn saw the vizier arriving upon-him, he-stood upon his-strength, and met-him, and greeted upon-him.
sentences.i: The vizier went in to the young man; and when Nūr al-Dīn saw the vizier coming toward him, he sprang to his feet, went to meet him, and greeted him.
sentences.n: نُورَالدِّينِ is printed as one word (Nūr al-Dīn) and is kept so. قَادِمٌ is left uninflected, as a loose circumstantial: Classical would have the accusative, 'saw the vizier coming'. عَلَى حَيْلِهِ (literally 'on his strength') is an idiom for rising briskly, on one's own feet.

sentences.t: فَرَحَّبَ بِهِ الْوَزِيرُ وَنَزَلَ مِنْ عَلَى جَوَادِهِ وَ احْتَضَنَهُ وَأَجْلَسَهُ عِنْدَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-raḥḥaba bihi al-wazīru wa-nazala min ʿalā jawādihi wa-iḥtaḍanahu wa-ajlasahu ʿindahu
sentences.l: So welcomed with-him the vizier, and descended from upon his-steed, and embraced-him, and seated-him by-him.
sentences.i: The vizier welcomed him warmly, got down from his horse, embraced him, and sat him beside him.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا وَلَدِي مِنْ أَيْنَ أَقْبَلْتَ وَمَاذَا تُرِيدُ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu yā waladī min ayna aqbalta wa-mādhā turīdu
sentences.l: And he-said to-him: O my-son, from where have-you-come, and what do-you-want?
sentences.i: He said to him, "My son, where have you come from, and what do you want?"

sentences.t: فَقَالَ نُورَالدِّينِ يَا مَوْلَايَ إِنِّي قَدِمْتُ مِنْ مَدِينَةِ مِصْرَ وَكُنْتُ ابْنَ وَزِيرٍ فِيهَا وَقَدِ انْتَقَلَ أَبِي إِلَى رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
sentences.tr: fa-qāla Nūr al-Dīni yā mawlāya innī qadimtu min madīnati Miṣra wa-kuntu ibna wazīrin fīhā wa-qadi intaqala abī ilā raḥmati Allāhi taʿālā
sentences.l: So Nūr al-Dīn said: O my-master, indeed-I came from the city of-Egypt, and I-was the-son of-a-vizier in-it, and my-father has-moved to the-mercy of-God, exalted-is-He.
sentences.i: Nūr al-Dīn said, "My lord, I have come from the city of Egypt, where I was a vizier's son; my father has passed to the mercy of God Most High."
sentences.n: انْتَقَلَ إِلَى رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ ('moved to God's mercy') is the courteous way to say that someone has died. مَدِينَةِ مِصْرَ is Cairo/Egypt: مِصْر names both the country and its capital.

sentences.t: وَأَخْبَرَهُ بِمَا جَرَى لَهُ مِنَ الْمُبْتَدَأِ إِلَى الْمُنْتَهَى
sentences.tr: wa-akhbarahu bi-mā jarā lahu mina al-mubtadaʾi ilā al-muntahā
sentences.l: And he-informed-him with what happened to-him from the beginning to the end.
sentences.i: And he told him all that had happened to him, from beginning to end.
sentences.n: الْمُبْتَدَا is printed without its final hamza (for الْمُبْتَدَأ); it is pointed here with the hamza restored over the alif, reading al-mubtadaʾ, 'the beginning'.

sentences.t: قَالَ وَقَدْ عَزَمْتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي أَنِّي لَا أَعُودُ أَبَدًا حَتَّى أَشُقَّ جَمِيعَ الْمُدُنِ وَالْبُلْدَانِ
sentences.tr: qāla wa-qad ʿazamtu ʿalā nafsī annī lā aʿūdu abadan ḥattā ashuqqa jamīʿa al-mudun wa-al-buldāni
sentences.l: He-said: And I-have resolved upon myself that-I not return ever until I-cleave all the-cities and-the-lands.
sentences.i: He said, "I have resolved within myself that I will never go back until I have crossed every city and land."
sentences.n: عَزَمْتُ عَلَى نَفْسِي is 'I made up my mind'. أَنِّي لَا أَعُودُ keeps the indicative after أَنَّ, as the text has it. أَشُقَّ is literally 'split, cleave'; with cities and lands it means to cut a path through them, that is, to traverse them.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْوَزِيرُ كَلَامَهُ قَالَ لَهُ وَلَدِي لَاتُطَاوِعِ النَّفْسَ فَتَرْمِيَكَ فِى الْهَلَاكِ فَإِنَّ الْبِلَادَ خَرَابٌ وَأَنَا أَخَافُ عَلَيْكَ مِنْ عَوَاقِبِ الزَّمَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-wazīru kalāmahu qāla lahu waladī lātuṭāwiʿi al-nafsa fa-tarmiyaka fī al-halāki fa-inna al-bilāda kharābun wa-anā akhāfu ʿalayka min ʿawāqibi al-zamāni
sentences.l: So when the vizier heard his-speech, he-said to-him: My-son, do-not obey the-soul, lest-it cast-you into the-destruction; for the-lands are ruin, and I fear for-you from the-consequences of-time.
sentences.i: When the vizier heard his words, he said, "My son, do not give in to your own desire, or it will throw you into ruin; the lands are desolate, and I fear for you what time may bring."
sentences.n: لَاتُطَاوِعِ is printed joined (لا تطاوع). النَّفْسَ is the self with its desires: 'do not obey your soul'. فَتَرْمِيَكَ is subjunctive after فَـ of consequence ('lest it throw you').

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ حَمَلَ خُرْجَهُ عَلَى بَغْلَتِهِ وَأَخَذَ الْبِسَاطَ وَالسَّجَّادَةَ وَأَخَذَ نُورَالدِّينِ مَعَهُ إِلَى بَيْتِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu ḥamala khurjahu ʿalā baghlatihi wa-akhadha al-bisāṭa wa-al-sajjādata wa-akhadha Nūr al-Dīni maʿahu ilā baytihi
sentences.l: Then indeed-he loaded his-saddlebag upon his-mule, and took the-carpet and the-prayer-rug, and took Nūr al-Dīn with-him to his-house.
sentences.i: Then he loaded the saddlebag onto the mule, took the carpet and the prayer rug, and brought Nūr al-Dīn home with him.
sentences.n: خُرْجَهُ is read as khurj, 'saddlebag', and the pronoun as the young man's; the Arabic does not say whose, and the vizier's own is possible. The carpet and prayer rug are Nur al-Din's belongings from earlier in the tale.

sentences.t: وَأَنْزَلَهُ فِي مَكَانٍ ظَرِيفٍ وَأَكْرَمَهُ وَأَحْسَنَ إِلَيْهِ وَحَبَّهُ حُبًّا شَدِيدًا
sentences.tr: wa-anzalahu fī makānin ẓarīfin wa-akramahu wa-aḥsana ilayhi wa-ḥabbahu ḥubban shadīdan
sentences.l: And he-lodged-him in a-place elegant, and honoured-him, and did-good to-him, and loved-him a-love intense.
sentences.i: He lodged him in a pleasant place, honoured him, treated him kindly, and loved him dearly.
sentences.n: وَحَبَّهُ is read as the simple verb ḥabba, 'to love', with a direct object, where Classical would use the causative أَحَبَّهُ; this is a Middle Arabic form, and it is vocalised as printed. حُبًّا شَدِيدًا is a cognate accusative: 'he loved him a strong love'.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ لَهُ يَا وَلَدِي أَنَا بَقِيتُ رَجُلًا كَبِيرًا وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لِي وَلَدٌ ذَكَرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla lahu yā waladī anā baqītu rajulan kabīran wa-lam yakun lī waladun dhakarun
sentences.l: And he-said to-him: O my-son, I have-become a-man great, and there-was-not to-me a-child male.
sentences.i: He said to him, "My son, I have grown to be an old man, and I have no son."
sentences.n: بَقِيتُ رَجُلًا كَبِيرًا uses بَقِيَ as 'become', 'have turned into', a Middle Arabic sense; كَبِير here means advanced in years. وَلَدٌ ذَكَرٌ is 'a male child', that is, a son.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ رَزَقَنِي اللَّهُ بِنْتًا تُعَادِلُكَ فِى الْحُسْنِ وَمُنِعَتْ عَنْهَا خُطَّابٌ كَثِيرٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qad razaqanī Allāhu bintan tuʿādiluka fī al-ḥusni wa-muniʿat ʿanhā khuṭṭābun kathīrun
sentences.l: And God has-provided-me a-daughter equalling-you in beauty, and were-kept-away from-her suitors many.
sentences.i: God has granted me a daughter who equals you in beauty, and many suitors have been kept away from her.
sentences.n: وَمُنِعَتْ is read as a passive with the broken plural خُطَّابٌ ('suitors') as subject; the print could equally be active, 'I kept many suitors from her', but then the noun would need to be accusative.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ وَقَعَ حُبُّكَ فِي قَلْبِي فَهَلْ لَكَ أَنْ تَقْبَلَ ابْنَتِي جَارِيَةً لِخِدْمَتِكَ وَتَكُونَ لَهَا بَعْلًا
sentences.tr: wa-qad waqaʿa ḥubbuka fī qalbī fa-hal laka an taqbala ibnatī jāriyatan li-khidmatika wa-takūna lahā baʿlan
sentences.l: And your-love has-fallen in my-heart; so is-there for-you that you-accept my-daughter, a-girl for-your-service, and you-be to-her a-husband?
sentences.i: Love for you has fallen into my heart; will you take my daughter as a handmaid to serve you, and be a husband to her?
sentences.n: فَهَلْ لَكَ أَنْ is a polite offer: 'is it for you (to accept) that...?', 'would you be willing to...'. جَارِيَةً لِخِدْمَتِكَ ('a girl for your service') puts the offer in the humblest terms, as is conventional in a marriage proposal.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَقْبَلُ ذَلِكَ أَطْلَعُ بِكَ إِلَى سُلْطَانِ الْبَصْرَةِ وَأَقُولُلَهُ أَنَّهُ وَلَدُ أَخِي وَأُوصِلُكَ إِلَى أَنْ أَجْعَلَكَ وَزِيرَهُ مَكَانِي وَأَلْزَمَ أَنَا بَيْتِي فَإِنِّي بَقِيتُ رَجُلًا كَبِيرًا
sentences.tr: fa-in kunta taqbalu dhālika aṭlaʿu bika ilā sulṭāni al-Baṣrati wa-aqūlulahu annahu waladu akhī wa-uwṣiluka ilā an ajʿalaka wazīrahu makānī wa-alzama anā baytī fa-innī baqītu rajulan kabīran
sentences.l: So if you-are accepting that, I-go-up with-you to the-sultan of-Basra and-I-say-to-him that-he (is) the-son of-my-brother, and I-bring-you to that I-make-you his-vizier in-my-place, and I-keep, I, my-house; for I have-become a-man great.
sentences.i: If you accept that, I will take you up to the sultan of Basra and tell him that you are my brother's son; and I will bring you to the point where I make you his vizier in my place, while I stay in my house, for I have grown old.
sentences.n: وَأَقُولُلَهُ is printed as one word, أَقُولُ لَهُ 'I say to him'. أَطْلَعُ بِكَ is 'I take you up', with بِـ marking the person taken, as with other verbs of conveying. وَأَلْزَمَ continues the subjunctive after أَنْ.
