sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ نُورَالدِّينِ كَلَامَ وَزِيرِالْبَصْرَةِ أَطْرَقَ بِرَأْسِهِ وَقَالَ سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa Nūr al-Dīni kalāma wazīri al-Baṣrati aṭraqa bi-raʾsihi wa-qāla samʿan wa-ṭāʿatan
sentences.l: So when Nūr al-Dīn heard the-speech of-the-vizier-of-Basra, he-lowered with-his-head and said: Hearing and obedience.
sentences.i: When Nūr al-Dīn heard the words of the vizier of Basra, he bowed his head and said, "With hearing and obedience."
sentences.n: وَزِيرِالْبَصْرَةِ is printed as one word. أَطْرَقَ بِرَأْسِهِ is 'he lowered his head'; the بِـ is optional here. سَمْعًا وَطَاعَةً is the stock formula of acceptance, an accusative of manner: '(I answer) with hearing and obedience'.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الْوَزِيرُ وَأَمَرَ غِلْمَانَهُ أَنْ يَضَعُوا لَهُ طَعَامًا وَأَنْ يُزَيِّنُواقَاعَةَ الْجُلُوسِ الْكَبِيرَةَ الَّتِي تُرْسَمُ فِيهَا أَعْرَاسُالْأُمَرَاءِ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-wazīru wa-amara ghilmānahu an yaḍaʿū lahu ṭaʿāman wa-an yuzayyinū qāʿata al-julūsi al-kabīrata allatī tursamu fīhā aʿrāsu al-umarāʾi
sentences.l: So the-vizier rejoiced, and commanded his-servants that they-set for-him food, and that they-adorn the-hall of-sitting the-great, which are-ordained in-it the-weddings of-the-princes.
sentences.i: The vizier was glad, and ordered his servants to lay out food for him and to deck the great sitting-hall, where the weddings of the princes are held.
sentences.n: يُزَيِّنُواقَاعَةَ and أَعْرَاسُالْأُمَرَاءِ are printed run together. تُرْسَمُ is read as the passive of رَسَمَ 'to ordain, prescribe': the hall in which princes' weddings are appointed to take place. The sense is clear, though the verb is slightly unusual.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَمَعَ أَصْحَابَهُ وَدَعَا أَكَابِرَ الدَّوْلَةِ وَتُجَّارَ الْبَصْرَةِ فَحَضَرُوا بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: thumma jamaʿa aṣḥābahu wa-daʿā akābira al-dawlati wa-tujjāra al-Baṣrati fa-ḥaḍarū bayna yadayhi
sentences.l: Then he-gathered his-companions, and invited the-great-ones of-the-state and the-merchants of-Basra, and they-attended between his-two-hands.
sentences.i: Then he gathered his friends, and invited the nobles of the realm and the merchants of Basra, and they came and stood before him.
sentences.n: بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ ('between his two hands') means 'in his presence, before him'.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُمْ إِنِّي كَانَ لِي أَخٌ وَزِيرٌ بِالدِّيَارِ الْمِصْرِيَّةِ وَرَزَقَهُ اللَّهُ وَلَدَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahum innī kāna lī akhun wazīrun bi-al-diyāri al-miṣriyyati wa-razaqahu Allāhu waladayni
sentences.l: So he-said to-them: Indeed-I, there-was to-me a-brother, a-vizier in-the-lands the-Egyptian, and God-provided-him two-sons.
sentences.i: He said to them, "I had a brother who was a vizier in the lands of Egypt, and God gave him two sons.
sentences.n: إِنِّي كَانَ لِي أَخٌ puts the pronoun up front and then restates it with لِي; the order is loose, a colloquial habit. The vizier's speech runs on through the next four sentences, to the point where the guests answer.

sentences.t: وَأَنَا كَمَا تَعْلَمُونَ رَزَقَنِي اللَّهُ بِنْتًا وَكَانَ أَخِي أَوْصَانِي أَنِّي أُزَوِّجُ بِنْتِي لِأَحَدِ أَوْلَادِهِ فَأَجَبْتُهُ لِذَلِكَ
sentences.tr: wa-anā ka-mā taʿlamūna razaqanī Allāhu bintan wa-kāna akhī awṣānī annī uzawwiju bintī li-aḥadi awlādihi fa-ajabtuhu li-dhālika
sentences.l: And I, as you-know, God-provided-me a-daughter; and my-brother had-charged-me that-I marry-off my-daughter to-one of-his-sons, so I-answered-him to that.
sentences.i: As you know, God gave me a daughter; and my brother had charged me to marry her to one of his sons, and I agreed to it.
sentences.n: أَنِّي أُزَوِّجُ is again indicative after أَنَّ ('that I marry off'), as the text has it. أَوْصَانِي أَنِّي: وَصَّى/أَوْصَى takes the thing charged as a clause.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا اسْتَحَقَّ الزَّوَاجَ أَرْسَلَ إِلَيَّ أَحَدَ أَوْلَادِهِ وَهُوَ هَذَا الشَّابُّ الْحَاضِرُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā istaḥaqqa al-zawāja arsala ilayya aḥada awlādihi wa-huwa hādhā al-shābbu al-ḥāḍiru
sentences.l: So when the-marriage fell-due, he-sent to-me one of-his-sons, and he (is) this youth the-present.
sentences.i: When the time for the marriage came, he sent me one of his sons, and he is this young man here present.
sentences.n: اسْتَحَقَّ الزَّوَاجَ, 'he (the son) deserved / came to merit marriage', is read as the son having come of age to marry; the Arabic does not mark the subject, which could also be the brother. هَذَا الشَّابُّ الْحَاضِرُ points to Nur al-Din, who is in the hall.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّاجَاءَنِي جِئْتُ أَنْ أَكْتُبَ كِتَابَهُ عَلَى بِنْتِي وَيَدْخُلَ بِهَا عِنْدِي وَهُوَ أَوْلَى مِنَ الْغَرِيبِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā jāʾanī jiʾtu an aktuba kitābahu ʿalā bintī wa-yadkhula bihā ʿindī wa-huwa awlā mina al-gharībi
sentences.l: So when he-came-to-me, I-set-about that I-write his-contract upon my-daughter, and that-he-go-in with-her at-me; and he (is) more-fitting than the-stranger.
sentences.i: When he came to me, I set about drawing up his marriage contract with my daughter, so that he may consummate it in my house; and he is a better choice than a stranger.
sentences.n: فَلَمَّاجَاءَنِي is printed as one word. جِئْتُ أَنْ أَكْتُبَ ('I came to write') means 'I undertook, I set about writing'. كَتَبَ كِتَابَهُ عَلَى is the idiom for drawing up a marriage contract (عَقْد) for a bride. دَخَلَ بِهَا, 'he entered with her', means he consummates the marriage.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ ذَلِكَ إِنْ شَاءَ يَقْعُدُ عِنْدِي وَإِنْ شَاءَ لِلسَّفَرِ أُسَيِّرُ هُوَ وَزَوْجَتُهُ إِلَى أَبِيهِ
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda dhālika in shāʾa yaqʿudu ʿindī wa-in shāʾa li-al-safari usayyiru huwa wa-zawjatuhu ilā abīhi
sentences.l: And after that, if he-wishes he-sits at-me, and if he-wishes, for the-travel, I-dispatch he and-his-wife to his-father.
sentences.i: And after that, if he wishes he may stay with me, and if he wishes to travel, I will send him and his wife on to his father."
sentences.n: The print gives اسير, which I read as أُسَيِّرُ, 'I send off', with هُوَ وَزَوْجَتُهُ as a loosely attached object (Middle Arabic often uses the subject pronoun for the object). It may also be a slip for يَسِيرُ, 'he and his wife travel', with much the same sense.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا جَمِيعًا نِعْمَ مَا رَأَيْتَ وَنَظَرُوا إِلَى الشَّابِّ فَلَمَّا رَأَوْهُ أَعْجَبَهُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū jamīʿan niʿma mā raʾayta wa-naẓarū ilā al-shābbi fa-lammā raʾawhu aʿjabahum
sentences.l: So they-said all-together: Excellent what you-have-judged! And they-looked at the youth, and when they-saw-him he-pleased-them.
sentences.i: They all said, "What you have decided is excellent." They looked at the young man, and when they saw him they were pleased with him.
sentences.n: نِعْمَ مَا رَأَيْتَ, 'excellent is what you have seen (judged fit)', is a set phrase of approval; رَأَى here is 'to think proper, to decide'.

sentences.t: فَأَحْضَرَ الْوَزِيرُ الشُّهُودَ وَالْقُضَاةَ وَكَتَبُوا الْكِتَابَ وَأَطْلَقُوا الْبَخُورَ وَشَرِبُوا السُّكَّرَ وَرَشُّوا الْمَاءَ وَرْدٍ وَانْصَرَفُوا
sentences.tr: fa-aḥḍara al-wazīru al-shuhūda wa-al-quḍāta wa-katabū al-kitāba wa-aṭlaqū al-bakhūra wa-sharibū al-sukkara wa-rashshū al-māʾa wardin wa-inṣarafū
sentences.l: So the-vizier brought-present the-witnesses and the-judges, and they-wrote the-contract, and released the-incense, and drank the-sugar, and sprinkled the-water of-rose, and departed.
sentences.i: The vizier summoned the witnesses and the judges; they wrote out the contract, burned incense, drank sweet sherbet, sprinkled rose-water, and went away.
sentences.n: أَطْلَقُوا الْبَخُورَ ('they released the incense') means they set the incense burning. شَرِبُوا السُّكَّرَ, 'drank the sugar', refers to sweetened drinks (sherbet) served at a wedding. الْمَاءَ وَرْدٍ is rose-water, in the form 'water of rose'.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا الْوَزِيرُ فَأَمَرَ غِلْمَانَهُ أَنْ يَأْخُذُوا نُورَالدِّينِ وَيُدْخِلُوا بِهِ الْحَمَّامَ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā al-wazīru fa-amara ghilmānahu an yaʾkhudhū Nūr al-Dīni wa-yudkhilū bihi al-ḥammāma
sentences.l: And as-for the-vizier, he-commanded his-servants that they-take Nūr al-Dīn and bring with-him into-the-bath.
sentences.i: As for the vizier, he ordered his servants to take Nūr al-Dīn and bring him into the bath.
sentences.n: وَأَمَّا ... فَـ ('as for ...') marks a change of subject. أَدْخَلَ بِهِ is 'to bring (someone) in', with بِـ marking the person led in.

sentences.t: وَأَعْطَاهُ الْوَزِيرُ بِدْلَةً مِنْ خَاصِّ مَلْبُوسِهِ وَأَرْسَلَ لَهُ الْمَنَاشِفَ وَالطَّاسَاتِ وَمَجَامِرَ الْبَخُورِ وَمَا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ
sentences.tr: wa-aʿṭāhu al-wazīru bidlatan min khāṣṣi malbūsihi wa-arsala lahu al-manāshifa wa-al-ṭāsāti wa-majāmira al-bakhūri wa-mā yaḥtāju ilayhi
sentences.l: And the-vizier gave-him a-suit from the-choice of-his-clothing, and sent to-him the-towels and the-bowls and the-censers of-incense and what one-needs of-it.
sentences.i: The vizier gave him a suit from his own finest clothes, and sent him towels, bowls, incense burners, and whatever else he needed.
sentences.n: بِدْلَةً is a suit of clothes. مِنْ خَاصِّ مَلْبُوسِهِ is 'from the choicest of what he wore'. يَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ: the verb takes إِلَى, 'to need (something)'.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّاخَرَجَ وَلَبِسَ الْبِدْلَةَ صَارَ كَالْبَدْرِ إِذَا بَدَرَ لَيْلَةَ أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kharaja wa-labisa al-bidlata ṣāra ka-al-badri idhā badara laylata arbaʿata ʿashara
sentences.l: So when he-came-out and wore the-suit, he-became like-the-full-moon when it-appears the-night of fourteen.
sentences.i: When he came out and put on the suit, he looked like the full moon when it rises on the fourteenth night.
sentences.n: فَلَمَّاخَرَجَ is printed as one word. صَارَ كَالْبَدْرِ ('became like the full moon') is a stock image of beauty. لَيْلَةَ أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ is the night of the 14th of the lunar month, when the moon is full.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا خَرَجَ مِنَ الْحَمَّامِ رَكِبَ بَغْلَتَهُ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ سَائِرًا حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى قَصْرِ الْوَزِيرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kharaja mina al-ḥammāmi rakiba baghlatahu wa-lam yazal sāʾiran ḥattā waṣala ilā qaṣri al-wazīri
sentences.l: So when he-came-out from the-bath, he-rode his-mule, and not he-ceased travelling until he-arrived at the-palace of-the-vizier.
sentences.i: When he came out of the bath, he mounted his mule and rode on until he reached the vizier's palace.
sentences.n: وَلَمْ يَزَلْ سَائِرًا ('and he did not cease going') is the usual way to say 'he kept on going'.

sentences.t: فَنَزَلَ عَنِ الْبَغْلَةِ وَدَخَلَ عَلَى الْوَزِيرِ فَقَبَّلَ يَدَيْهِ وَرَحَّبَ بِهِ
sentences.tr: fa-nazala ʿani al-baghlati wa-dakhala ʿalā al-wazīri fa-qabbala yadayhi wa-raḥḥaba bihi
sentences.l: So he-dismounted from the-mule, and entered upon the-vizier, and kissed his-two-hands, and he-welcomed with-him.
sentences.i: He dismounted from the mule and went in to the vizier and kissed his hands, and the vizier welcomed him.
sentences.n: The subject of وَرَحَّبَ بِهِ switches to the vizier: 'and (he) welcomed him'; the Arabic leaves the change unmarked.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka Shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the-morning overtook Shahrazad, so she-fell-silent from the-speech the-permitted.
sentences.i: And morning overtook Shahrazad, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
sentences.n: This is the stock formula that ends each night: dawn overtakes Shahrazad and she stops her 'permitted' (allowable) storytelling.
